items.content:
지난주 AI 산업의 부채 문제가 불거지면서 세계 금융시장이 흔들렸습니다. 특히 AI 클라우드 업체 코어위브의 주가와 채권 가격이 급락하면서 AI 인프라 투자에 대한 경고가 쏟아졌습니다. 그런데 이 과정에서 눈길을 끈 인물은 코어위브 경영진이 아닌 젠슨 황 엔비디아 CEO였습니다.

그는 지난 15일(현지시간) 스웨덴 스톡홀름에서 코어위브의 재무 상태가 매일 개선되고 있다며 투자자들을 안심시켰습니다. 다음 날 독일 베를린에서도 AI 시장의 혼란에 대해 "이 모든 것은 지나갈 것"이라며 낙관적인 전망을 내놨습니다.

세계 최대 AI 반도체 기업의 CEO가 한 클라우드 업체의 재무 상태까지 직접 설명한 것은 눈길을 끄는 대목입니다. 그리고 그 이유는 엔비디아가 지난 몇 년간 네오클라우드라는 새로운 시장을 키워온 전략과 관련이 있습니다.

네오클라우드는 엔비디아의 GPU를 대량으로 확보해 AI 개발사나 기업에 컴퓨팅 자원을 빌려주는 업체입니다. 코어위브가 대표적입니다. 2017년 암호화폐 채굴 사업으로 출발한 코어위브는 2023년 생성 AI 열풍을 타고 GPU 클라우드 사업을 빠르게 키웠습니다.

이 과정에서 엔비디아는 최신 GPU를 공급하고 자금을 지원 하며 성장을 도왔습니다. 올해 1월에도 20억달러를 추가 투자했으며, 코어위브 지분 약 10%를 보유하고 있습니다. 2030년까지 5기가와트(GW) 규모의 AI 데이터센터를 구축하는 사업에도 협력하고 있습니다.

엔비디아가 코어위브를 이처럼 지원한 데에는 이유가 있습니다. 엔비디아는 AI 붐으로 막대한 돈을 벌어들였지만, 매출의 상당 부분을 MS와 아마존, 구글 등 소수의 대형 고객에게 의존 하고 있습니다.

문제는 이들이 엔비디아의 주요 고객인 동시에 잠재적인 경쟁자라는 점입니다. 엔비디아 GPU는 성능이 뛰어나지만, 가격도 비쌉니다. 따라서 자금력과 기술력을 갖춘 대형 클라우드 기업들은 자체 AI 칩을 개발하며 엔비디아에 대한 의존도를 낮추려고 합니다.

엔비디아로서는 장기적으로 GPU 판매를 유지하려면 이들 외에도 대규모 구매자를 확보할 필요가 있습니다. 네오클라우드가 바로 그런 역할을 합니다. 이들은 엔비디아 GPU를 사업의 핵심 자산으로 사용하며, 자체 AI 칩을 개발해 엔비디아와 경쟁할 가능성도 상대적으로 작습니다.

코어위브처럼 네오클라우드가 성장할수록 엔비디아는 대형 고객에 대한 의존도를 낮추고 새로운 GPU 수요를 확보할 수 있는 것입니다. 실제로 엔비디아의 지난 7월 분기 데이터센터 매출 중 대형 클라우드 기업을 제외한 고객의 비중은 45%에 달했습니다. 여기에는 네오클라우드뿐 아니라 일반 기업도 포함됩니다.

엔비디아가 지원한 업체도 코어위브뿐만이 아닙니다. 네비우스와 엔스케일 등 여러 네오클라우드 업체에 투자하거나 사업 구축을 지원해 왔습니다. 20일 등장한 분석 에 따르면 엔비디아가 데이터센터 사업을 지원하기 위해 제공한 보증과 컴퓨팅 용량 구매 약정 등은 지난 7월 분기 기준 최대 1645억달러에 달합니다. 이와 별도로 AI 클라우드 업체에 투자했거나 투자하기로 약속한 금액도 70억달러가 넘습니다. 직접 투자와 보증, 구매 약정 등을 합쳐 1700억달러 이상을 AI 인프라 시장에 걸어둔 셈입니다

그러나 이제 상황이 달라지고 있습니다. 디 인포메이션은 지난 18일 업계 경영진들을 인용해 현재 수백개에 달하는 네오클라우드 업체 중 몇 년 뒤에는 7~10개만 남을 수 있다는 전망을 전했습니다. GPU 확보와 데이터센터 건설에 막대한 돈이 들어가는 데다 경쟁까지 치열해지면서 상당수 업체가 독자적으로 살아남기 어렵다는 것입니다.

최근 코어위브 사태는 이런 위험을 보여준 사례입니다. 금융시장에서도 AI 기업들이 빚을 갚지 못할 가능성에 대비하는 거래가 급증했습니다. 파이낸셜타임스(FT) 에 따르면 주요 기술 기업의 채무불이행 위험에 대비하는 파생상품 거래 규모는 지난 7월 주간 20억달러 미만에서 9월에는 90억달러 이상으로 늘었습니다.

그렇다고 AI 컴퓨팅 수요 자체가 사라졌다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 코어위브 역시 당장 채무 상환 위기에 몰린 것은 아니며, 장기 계약을 바탕으로 사업을 운영하고 있습니다. 문제는 앞으로도 막대한 자금을 조달하며 사업을 키울 수 있느냐는 것입니다.

여기서 엔비디아의 고민이 시작됩니다. 네오클라우드 기업들이 잇달아 무너지면 공들여 키워온 GPU 판매처도 줄어들기 때문입니다. 특히 데이터센터를 직접 건설하는 업체들이 자금난으로 사업을 중단하면 GPU를 공급할 새로운 시설의 건설까지 차질을 빚을 수 있습니다.

월스트리트저널(WSJ) 은 20일 코어위브의 사업 모델이 흔들릴 때 엔비디아가 구제에 나설 강력한 경제적 이유가 있다고 분석했습니다. 다만 젠슨 황은 공식적으로 코어위브에 대한 추가 구제 지원이 필요하지 않다는 입장을 밝힌 바 있습니다.

그런 가운데 엔비디아가 이달 초 기업공개(IPO)를 철회한 호주 네오클라우드 업체 퍼머스 에 수억달러를 추가 투자하는 방안을 논의 중이라는 보도도 20일 나왔습니다.

이처럼 GPU 공급을 넘어 고객의 사업과 자금 조달까지 지원하고 있습니다. AI 산업의 '중앙은행' 이라는 비유도 나왔습니다. GPU를 판매하려면 이를 구매할 기업들이 필요하고, 그 기업들이 성장하려면 다시 엔비디아의 지원이 필요한 관계가 만들어진 셈입니다.

결국 코어위브 사태는 엔비디아에도 남의 일이 아닙니다. 네오클라우드 시장에 대규모 구조조정이 시작된다면 그동안 키워온 고객들을 어디까지 지원할 것인지 선택해야 할 수 있습니다. 젠슨 황이 지난주 직접 시장을 안심시키려 했던 이유도 이런 이해관계에서 찾을 수 있을 것입니다.

■ 앤트로픽, ‘숨은 의도 읽는’ 새 모델 준비...구글·오픈AI도 후속작 예고

구글과 오픈AI의 차세대 모델에 대한 소식이 잇따르는 가운데, 앤트로픽도 새로운 모델을 준비 중이라는 구체적인 정보가 나왔습니다. 특히 사용자가 명확하게 설명하지 않아도 숨은 의도와 목표를 파악하는 능력이 강조됐는데, 이는 과거 오픈AI를 비롯한 AI 기업들이 모델의 성능이 크게 도약할 때마다 내세웠던 특징이기도 합니다.

국내 AI 인프라 기업 엘리스그룹이 코스닥 상장 첫날 공모가보다 32% 하락하며 코어위브발 투자심리 악화의 영향을 받은 것으로 풀이됩니다. 래블업과 슈퍼브에이아이 등도 상장을 추진하고 있어 AI 인프라 기업에 대한 시장의 평가가 주목됩니다.

■ 머스크 “미국 모든 어린이에게 스페이스X 주식 1주씩”…14조원 규모

머스크가 앤트로픽의 회사 지분 5% 공익 기금 출연 발표에 대응해 내년 미국의 모든 어린이에게 스페이스X 주식을 1주씩 나눠주겠다고 약속했습니다. 약 14조원 규모로, 실제 이행된다면 수천만명의 어린이를 주주로 확보하면서 장기적으로 상당한 홍보 효과를 거둘 수도 있습니다.

items.content:
오픈AI가 구글 클라우드를 통해 최신 AI 모델과 코딩 에이전트 ‘코덱스’를 판매한다. 챗GPT와 제미나이로 경쟁하는 두 회사가 기업 시장에서는 판매 협력에 나선 것이다. 오픈AI는 구글의 기업 고객에게 접근할 통로를 확보하고, 구글은 자사 모델뿐 아니라 경쟁사 모델을 원하는 고객까지 클라우드에 붙잡아 두겠다는 전략이다.

양사는 21일(현지시간) 공식 발표를 통해 오픈AI의 첨단 모델과 '코덱스'를 구글 클라우드의 AI 모델 제공 플랫폼 ‘모델 가든’에 도입한다고 밝혔다. 일부 기업 고객을 대상으로 비공개 프리뷰를 시작했으며, 몇주 내 정식 제공할 예정이다.

초기 제공 모델은 'GPT-6 아스트라'와 ‘GPT-6.1 솔’, ‘GPT-6 루나’다. 기업은 작업의 난도와 비용, 응답 속도에 맞춰 모델을 선택할 수 있다.

개발자는 코덱스의 명령줄 도구(CLI)와 데스크톱 앱을 구글 클라우드에 연결해 사용할 수 있으며, 향후 구글의 코딩 도구 ‘안티그래비티’와 기업용 AI 서비스에도 오픈AI 모델이 들어갈 예정이다.

사업적으로 중요한 부분은 결제 방식이다. 기업은 구글 클라우드 마켓플레이스에서 오픈AI 모델을 구매하고, 해당 사용료를 기존에 약정한 구글 클라우드 지출액에 포함할 수 있다. 구글에 일정 금액을 쓰기로 계약한 기업이 그 예산으로 오픈AI 모델까지 이용할 수 있다는 뜻이다.

사용료도 구글 클라우드 청구서에 통합된다. 오픈AI를 도입하기 위해 별도 공급사 계약과 구매 절차를 거쳐야 하는 부담을 줄이는 구조다.

보안과 데이터 관리도 기업 공략의 핵심이다. 양사는 구글 클라우드의 접근 권한 관리와 데이터 관리 체계를 오픈AI 모델 이용에 적용한다고 설명했다.

구글은 고객의 입력과 출력 데이터를 기반 모델 학습에 사용하지 않고, 고객이 모델 이용 기록을 기존 클라우드 환경에서 통합 관리·점검할 수 있도록 한다고 밝혔다. 금융과 의료 등 데이터 취급 규정이 엄격한 업종의 도입을 겨냥한 조치다.

오픈AI에는 마이크로소프트(MS) 중심이던 기업 판매망을 넓힌다는 의미가 있다. 이번 협력으로 오픈AI는 MS와 아마존웹서비스(AWS), 구글 클라우드 등 미국 3대 클라우드를 모두 판매 통로로 확보하게 됐다.

지난 4월 MS와의 독점 유통 관계가 해제된 뒤 AWS에 진출했고, 이번에 구글까지 합류했다. 기업이 쓰던 클라우드를 바꾸도록 설득하는 대신, 기업이 이미 사용하는 환경에 모델을 공급하게 됐다.

오픈AI는 이번 발표 말미에 MS가 여전히 자사의 주요 클라우드 파트너라고 명시했다.

구글에도 경쟁사 모델을 판매할 이유가 있다. 기업이 오픈AI 모델을 선택하더라도 구매와 이용을 구글 클라우드 안에서 처리하도록 만들 수 있기 때문이다.

구글은 기존 '제미나이'와 앤트로픽의 '클로드'에 오픈AI 모델까지 추가하면서, 주요 3개사의 폐쇄형 모델을 모두 제공하는 유일한 대형 클라우드라고 강조했다. 모델 선택권을 넓혀 고객이 다른 클라우드로 옮길 유인을 줄이려는 전략이다. 토머스 쿠리안 구글 클라우드 CEO는 오픈AI를 포함한 다양한 모델을 제공해 고객이 작업에 적합한 모델을 선택하도록 돕겠다고 설명했다.

두 회사의 협력은 이번이 처음은 아니다. 구글은 지난해 오픈AI에 컴퓨팅 자원을 공급하는 계약을 맺었다. 당시에는 오픈AI가 구글의 클라우드 고객이었다면, 이번에는 구글이 오픈AI 모델의 판매까지 맡게 됐다. AI 서비스와 검색에서는 경쟁하면서 컴퓨팅 자원 공급과 기업 영업에서는 협력하는 관계로 접점이 늘어난 셈이다.

다만 판매망 확보가 곧바로 모델 선택으로 이어지는 것은 아니다. 오픈AI는 같은 플랫폼에 입점한 제미나이 및 클로드와 성능과 가격을 놓고 경쟁해야 한다.

items.title: 웹사이트 70% 쓰는 PHP서 AI가 결함 발견…각국 정부 사이트 중단
items.summary: AI가 웹사이트 구동에 널리 쓰이는 프로그래밍 언어 PHP에서 중대 보안 취약점을 찾아내면서 유럽 정부와 병원, 학교 등이 웹사이트를 잇달아 중단했다. 공격자가 서버를 장악할 수 있는 결함이 확인되자 피해를 막기 위해 접속부터 차단한 것이다. 긴급 수정본은 배포됐지만, 공격자 역시 AI로 이를 분석해 업데이트하지 않은 서버를 노릴 수 있어 대응 속도가 중요해졌다.월스트리트저널(WSJ)과 로이터, 블룸버그 등은 21일(현지시간) PHP에서 두 가지 심각한 취약점이 공개된 뒤 유럽 각국 정부와 기관들
items.content:
AI가 웹사이트 구동에 널리 쓰이는 프로그래밍 언어 PHP에서 중대 보안 취약점을 찾아내면서 유럽 정부와 병원, 학교 등이 웹사이트를 잇달아 중단했다. 공격자가 서버를 장악할 수 있는 결함이 확인되자 피해를 막기 위해 접속부터 차단한 것이다. 긴급 수정본은 배포됐지만, 공격자 역시 AI로 이를 분석해 업데이트하지 않은 서버를 노릴 수 있어 대응 속도가 중요해졌다.

월스트리트저널(WSJ)과 로이터, 블룸버그 등은 21일(현지시간) PHP에서 두 가지 심각한 취약점이 공개된 뒤 유럽 각국 정부와 기관들이 긴급 업데이트와 서비스 중단에 나섰다고 보도했다. 미국 정부도 연방기관과 주요 기반 시설을 보호하기 위해 기술 기업들과 보안 패치 적용을 지원하고 있다.

네덜란드에서는 정부 포털과 로테르담 항만, 축구협회, 주요 정당과 여러 병원의 대외 공개 웹사이트가 중단됐다. 현지 통신사 ANP에 따르면 소프트웨어업체 노투비즈의 서비스를 이용하는 지방자치단체와 주 정부, 물 관리기관 등 100곳 이상도 영향을 받았다.

덴마크에서는 학교 소통 플랫폼 등이 멈췄고, 핀란드와 독일, 프랑스도 정부 웹사이트를 일시 차단했다. 독일 프라이부르크대와 오스트리아 빈대, 위키미디어 재단과 인터넷 아카이브도 일부 사이트나 시스템을 중단했다.

이들 기관이 모두 해킹당한 것은 아니다. 독일과 핀란드는 예방 조치라고 설명했으며, 핀란드는 취약점 악용 시도나 데이터 유출 때문에 서비스를 중단한 것은 아니라고 밝혔다.

PHP는 웹사이트 서버에서 이용자의 요청을 처리하고 화면에 표시할 내용을 만드는 프로그래밍 언어다. 무료 오픈소스로 제공되며, 워드프레스와 드루팔, 줌라 등 웹사이트 제작·관리 도구의 기반으로 쓰인다.

서버 측 프로그래밍 언어를 확인할 수 있는 웹사이트의 약 70%가 PHP를 사용한다. 전체 웹사이트의 약 40%를 구동하는 워드프레스도 PHP에 의존한다. 여러 서비스가 함께 쓰는 기반 기술에서 결함이 발견돼 영향이 커진 것이다.

‘PHP2Shell’로 불리는 두 취약점은 특정 조건에서 계정이나 비밀번호 없이 서버에 명령을 실행할 수 있는 결함이다. 심각도는 각각 10점 만점에 9.2점으로 평가됐다. 공격에 성공하면 데이터를 훔치거나 웹페이지를 변조하고 시스템을 장악할 수 있다.

이번 발견에는 오픈AI와 구글의 AI 모델이 활용됐다. 보안업체 캘리프(Calif)는 ‘GPT-5.6 솔’을 활용해 취약점을 찾아 지난 8월 신고했다. 알파벳 산하 보안업체 위즈(Wiz)도 자체 AI 도구와 구글의 ‘제미나이 4 아르곤’, GPT-5.6 솔을 활용해 독립적으로 문제를 확인했다.

위즈에 따르면 결함은 10년 이상 PHP 코드에 남아 있었지만, 실제 공격으로 연결하는 과정이 매우 복잡했다. AI가 이 장벽을 낮췄다는 설명이다. 위즈는 “세계적인 연구팀이 몇 달에 걸쳐 수행했을 작업을 연구원 한 명이 일주일 만에 완료했다”고 밝혔다.

개발진은 문제의 징후를 알고도 수정을 마치지 못했다. PHP 재단은 2024년 취약점 하나의 징후를 발견했지만 구체적인 공격 경로를 확인하지 못했고, 수정 방식도 결정하지 못했다고 설명했다. 재단은 의사결정 과정과 자원 부족에 따른 “구조적 실패”라고 인정했다.

PHP 개발진은 취약점 관련 정보와 공격 시연 영상이 예정에 앞서 공개되자 배포일을 하루 당겨 21일 수정본을 내놨다. 그러나 수정본 공개는 공격자에게도 결함을 분석할 단서를 제공한다. 보안업체 TLP:블랙의 코스틴 라이우 공동창업자는 AI가 취약점 “악용 경쟁”을 부추기고 있다며 대규모 공격 가능성을 경고했다.

클라우드플레어는 이미 일부 초기 공격 시도를 관찰하고 고객 보호 조치를 도입했다고 밝혔다. 미국 사이버보안·인프라보안국(CISA)은 발표 시점까지 악용 사례를 확인하지 못했다고 전했다. 다만 실제 침입이나 데이터 유출 등 피해 규모는 아직 확인되지 않았다.

당장 필요한 조치는 PHP 사용 여부를 확인하고 서버에 수정본을 적용하는 것이다. 워드프레스의 일반적인 자동 업데이트만으로는 해결되지 않으며, 서버에 설치된 PHP 자체를 업데이트해야 한다.

미국 국가안보국(NSA)과 유럽 보안기관들은 즉시 업데이트하기 어렵다면 수정과 검증을 마칠 때까지 해당 시스템의 외부 접속을 차단하라고 권고했다. 영국 국가사이버보안센터(NCSC)는 이미 침입한 흔적이 있는지도 검사하라고 안내했다.

오래된 서버는 대응에 시간이 걸릴 수 있다. 인터넷 분석업체 센시스에 따르면 관측한 약 260만개 호스트 가운데 150만개가 수정본을 제공받기 어려운 PHP 버전을 사용하고 있었다.

공식 지원이 끝난 버전은 지원 중인 버전으로 전환하거나 공급업체의 별도 지원을 확인해야 한다. 수정본이 배포됐더라도 개별 서버에 적용되기 전까지는 공격 위험이 남는다.

items.title: [긴급] PHP ‘PHP2Shell’ 치명적 취약점 2건…인증 없이 원격 코드 실행 위험

items.content:
PHP에서 인증받지 않은 공격자가 원격으로 코드를 실행할 수 있는 치명적 취약점 2건이 공개됐다. 웹사이트 운영 조직은 서버에 설치된 PHP뿐 아니라 실제 웹 요청을 처리하는 실행 환경의 패치 적용 여부를 긴급 점검해야 한다.

PHP 개발팀은 10월 21일 ‘PHP2Shell’로 알려진 CVE-2026-109618과 CVE-2026-109619를 해결한 보안 업데이트를 공개하고 즉각적인 적용을 권고했다. 두 취약점의 심각도는 각각 CVSS 4.0 기준 9.2점이다. 수정 버전은 PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, 8.5.12다.

CVE-2026-109618은 메모리 부족 오류를 처리하는 과정에서 발생한다. 내부 요청 데이터의 초기화가 끝나기 전에 처리가 중단되면, 요청 종료 과정에서 잘못된 메모리 상태를 정상 데이터처럼 사용해 원격 코드 실행으로 이어질 수 있다. PHP 개발팀은 아파치 모듈인 mod_php의 일반적인 구성에서 인증되지 않은 HTTP 요청을 통한 코드 실행을 검증했다고 밝혔다. 이 경로는 웹 애플리케이션 코드가 실행되기 전에도 작동한다.

CVE-2026-109619는 요청 처리에 사용한 메모리가 해제된 뒤에도 내부 상태가 남는 문제다. 같은 작업 프로세스가 후속 요청을 처리하면서 오래된 상태를 참조해 코드 실행으로 이어질 수 있다. 두 취약점 모두 PHP 자체의 요청 처리와 관련돼 있어 개별 게시판이나 플러그인 업데이트만으로 대응을 완료해서는 안 된다.

PHP 개발팀은 PHP-FPM, 아파치 mod_php, PHP-CGI, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed 등 웹 요청을 처리하는 PHP 설치 환경을 위험 점검 대상으로 제시했다. 특히 mod_php의 위험을 가장 높게 평가했다. 다만 실행 방식과 구성에 따라 공격 조건이 달라지므로 모든 PHP 서버에서 동일한 방식으로 공격이 성공한다고 단정할 수는 없다.

운영자는 php -v 결과만으로 패치 여부를 판단하지 않도록 주의해야 한다. 이 명령은 명령행에서 호출되는 PHP의 버전을 보여주므로, 웹서비스가 별도의 PHP-FPM이나 아파치 모듈을 사용하는 환경에서는 실제 서비스 버전과 다를 수 있다. 가상호스트별 실행 환경, 컨테이너 이미지, 호스팅 사업자가 제공하는 PHP, 제품에 자체 내장된 PHP도 함께 확인해야 한다. 업데이트 이후에는 기존 작업 프로세스가 계속 동작하지 않도록 재시작 또는 컨테이너 재배포 여부까지 검증할 필요가 있다.

리눅스 배포판 패키지는 보안 수정사항을 기존 버전에 반영하는 ‘백포트’ 방식도 고려해야 한다. 예를 들어 우분투는 24.04 LTS의 수정 패키지로 8.3.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.13을 안내했다. 따라서 PHP의 기본 버전 숫자뿐 아니라 배포판의 전체 패키지 버전과 두 CVE의 수정 여부를 확인해야 한다.

즉시 업데이트하기 어려운 경우에도 설정 변경을 완전한 해결책으로 봐서는 안 된다. PHP 개발팀은 session.upload_progress.enabled=0 설정과 작업 프로세스 재시작이 확인된 일부 공격 경로를 차단하지만 다른 변형까지 막지는 못한다고 설명했다. PHP 8.5의 fatal_error_backtraces=0 설정 역시 특정 경로에 한정된 완화책이다. 근본 대응은 수정 버전 또는 공급업체가 보안 패치를 반영한 패키지를 실제 웹 실행 환경에 적용하는 것이다.

items.title: Google Chrome adds Gemini-powered scam detection, warns users of ClickFix attacks
items.summary: Chrome is getting new scam protections that use Gemini to detect deceptive websites and warn users when they copy suspicious commands from ClickFix attacks. [...]
items.content:
Google Chrome adds Gemini-powered scam detection, warns users of ClickFix attacks

Chrome is getting new scam protections that use Gemini to detect deceptive websites and warn users when they copy suspicious commands from ClickFix attacks.

The changes are part of Enhanced Protection in Safe Browsing, which Google claims makes users ten times safer from phishing, social engineering, notification abuse, and other scams compared with Standard Protection.

Chrome is also adding a new "suspicious site" warning for pages that show deceptive patterns but haven't reached the confidence level required for its existing full-page red warning.

"Suspicious site warnings notify users when a page exhibits deceptive patterns commonly associated with known malicious sites," the company explained .

"By tailoring the warning UI in this way, we are able to safely expand our coverage to display a higher volume of protective warnings."

Gemini is moving from on-device to server-side scam detection

Chrome previously used an on-device Gemini model to detect tech support scams, but it's now moving to a more powerful server-side model for Enhanced Protection users.

As explained by Google, the model looks at signals such as the brand represented on a page, its intent, and how likely it is to be a scam. Safe Browsing then combines that analysis with domain reputation and other security signals.

"Chrome minimizes the amount of data shared with the server by only analyzing page text when a site exhibits high-confidence scam indicators," Google noted.

"And whenever page content is sent off the device, it is processed ephemerally – meaning it is never logged, retained or used to train models."

Enhanced Protection can also detect when you copy a suspicious command from a ClickFix scam, which typically tricks users into running malicious PowerShell or Command Prompt commands themselves.

If Chrome suspects a ClickFix script, it removes personally identifiable information from the clipboard payload and sends it to Safe Browsing for analysis. If it comes back as dangerous, Chrome displays a warning before you continue.

Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked

Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

items.content:
뉴욕증시는 스페이스X를 비롯한 주요 기술 기업의 호실적에 힘입어 일제히 상승 마감했다. 최근 인공지능(AI) 투자 수익성에 대한 우려로 약세를 보이던 기술주가 반등하면서 나스닥지수는 1% 넘게 올랐다.

21일(현지시간) 뉴욕증권거래소(NYSE)에서 다우존스30 산업평균지수는 전장 대비 360.21포인트(0.69%) 오른 5만2856.09에 거래를 마쳤다.

스탠더드앤드푸어스(S&P)500지수는 44.60포인트(0.58%) 상승한 7757.17에, 기술주 중심의 나스닥종합지수는 278.04포인트(1.05%) 뛴 2만6702.86에 거래를 마쳤다.

이날 기술주 강세는 일론 머스크의 우주기업 스페이스X의 호실적이 이끌었다. 스페이스X는 상장 이후 처음으로 흑자를 기록했다고 발표했다. 이와 함께 머스크는 전기차 업체 테슬라와의 합병 가능성을 공식화했다. 이에 스페이스X는 7.79% 상승했고, 테슬라는 3.41% 올랐다.

AI 서버 제조업체 슈퍼마이크로컴퓨터는 AI 플랫폼 수요 증가를 이유로 시장 예상을 뛰어넘는 매출 전망을 제시하면서 주가가 9.55% 뛰었다.

다만 AI 투자 수익성에 대한 우려가 완전히 해소되지는 않은 모습이다. AI 클라우드 업체 코어위브는 장중 4% 가까이 급등했다가 4% 넘게 급락하는 등 큰 변동성을 보이다가 결국 0.5% 하락했다.

서상영 미래에셋증권 상무는 “미 증시는 스페이스X와 슈퍼마이크로컴퓨터의 분기 실적 발표로 AI 관련 주식에 대한 투자심리가 개선되며 상승 출발했으나 여전히 네오클라우드 기업을 중심으로 변화가 지속되며 관련 우려가 해소되지 못하고 있음을 보여주며 지수 상승을 제한했다”고 설명했다.

국제유가는 혼조세를 보였다. 중동 지역의 군사적 긴장 고조와 러시아·우크라이나 간 평화협상 재개 기대가 엇갈린 영향으로 풀이된다.

이날 런던 ICE선물거래소에서 12월 인도분 브렌트유 선물 종가는 배럴당 108.82달러로 전장 대비 0.03% 올랐다. 뉴욕상품거래소에서 12월 인도분 서부텍사스산원유(WTI) 선물 종가는 배럴당 97.15달러로 전장보다 0.68% 내렸다.

한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다.

사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다.

위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다.

한경닷컴 증권팀에서 국내 주식시장과 금융투자업계를 취재하고 있습니다. 독자에게 필요한 투자 정보를 빠르고 정확하게 전달하겠습니다. 기획연재 에서는 핵심 투자 상품으로 자리 잡은 ETF를 집중적으로 다룹니다.

items.summary: Banking advocacy organizations are pushing back against the OCC’s finalized rules on a stablecoin law, arguing against changes to provisions on yield.
items.content:
Banking advocacy organizations are pushing back against the OCC’s finalized rules on a stablecoin law, arguing against changes to provisions on yield.

A lobbying group for US banks has weighed in on the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency’s (OCC’s) recently finalized rules on payment stablecoin issuance and custody, arguing that the regulator’s interpretation went against Congress’ intent.

In a Wednesday notice, the American Bankers Association (ABA) said that while the OCC’s final rules implementing the GENIUS Act included “several positive steps,” the banking group remained critical of provisions related to stablecoin yield. The regulator dropped a provision that would have established a presumption that certain third-party arrangements violated the law’s ban on yield payments.

“The final rule removes the OCC’s originally proposed safeguards that would have addressed indirect arrangements involving affiliates, exchanges and other distribution partners,” said ABA. “As a result, payment stablecoin issuers can provide economically equivalent yield while technically avoiding the statutory prohibition. The OCC also declined to adopt a broader presumption against arrangements designed to circumvent the ban.”

Stablecoin rewards were one of the key issues lawmakers and interest groups debated before and after GENIUS passed Congress in July 2025, and they continue to face scrutiny amid discussions of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill currently in limbo after a failed procedure vote in the Senate last month.

Notably, the Blockchain Association approved of the change to yield prohibition, arguing that the OCC “[brought] the final rule more closely in line with the statutory text.” The Bank Policy Institute, another banking industry advocacy group, largely sided with ABA, saying that “the decision to omit the yield presumption replaces clarity with ambiguity and puts the banking system and its customers at risk of deposit flight.”

The OCC finalized its rules ahead of the GENIUS Act’s implementation in January 2027. Other government departments are expected to release rules on GENIUS related to their agencies’ purview over stablecoins, including the Federal Reserve and Treasury.

items.content:
Japan's Onamae Desktop Cloud hacked, up to 27,000 servers affected

Hackers compromised the infrastructure of Onamae Desktop Cloud, a popular provider of VPS services in Japan, and installed malware on up to 26,739 customers' servers.

The company confirmed on October 20 that an unauthorized third party installed "malicious programs" in some customer environments.

After detecting the intrusion, the company says it progressively shut down customer servers beginning at 04:00 local time on October 21, 2026.

“We have confirmed that unauthorized access by a third party occurred against Onamae.com Desktop Cloud and that unauthorized programs were installed in some customers’ server environments,” reads the announcement.

Onamae.com, operated by GMO Internet, a member of GMO Internet Group, is one of Japan’s largest domain registrars and also provides web hosting, DNS, and other internet infrastructure services.

Its Desktop Cloud byGMO service is advertised as "ideal for stable FX automated trading, including continuous operation of MetaTrader 4 (MT4)."

According to the alert, the breach may have exposed data stored on the impacted servers. However, the company has not confirmed any instance of information being misused or leaked.

The company also emphasizes that payment information, such as credit card details, is not affected because it is stored on a different infrastructure.

As the investigation continues and more details become available, GMO says it will provide updates.

The company announced a service interruption starting today at 4 a.m. (local time), noting that all Desktop Cloud plans will be impacted. No estimated date has been provided for restarting the service.

Customers who stored secrets, such as passwords, on their servers are advised to rotate them as soon as possible, as they may have been compromised.

The company also noted an increased risk of phishing emails and other unsolicited communications, as threat actors may try to exploit the incident to convince customers to disclose sensitive information.

“We will never ask you for your password or credit card information via email or phone,” the company says.

items.content:
삼양식품 의 3분기 실적 발표를 앞두고 증권가에서 '매수' 의견 보고서가 잇따랐다. 증권가에서 제시한 평균 목표주가는 186만원대로 현재 주가인 125만원대보다 약 49% 높다. 하반기 국내 증시 급락 속에서도 주가가 상승세를 지킨 저력과 함께 세계적으로 공전의 히트를 한 '불닭'의 해외 수요를 바탕으로 3분기 최대 실적을 거뒀을 것이란 분석이 나온다.

22일 금융투자업계에 따르면 이번주 들어서만 6개 증권사가 삼양식품에 대한 매수 리포트를 발표했다. 유안타증권이 목표주가 200만원을 제시했고 현대차·다올투자증권은 각각 190만원, 한국투자·키움증권은 각각 185만원, 한화투자증권은 180만원을 유지했다.

주가도 급락장에서 상대적으로 선방하고 있다. 삼양식품은 전날 전 거래일보다 2.70% 오른 125만4000원에 거래를 마쳤다. 지난 6월 말보다 12.06% 상승해 같은 기간 32.33% 떨어진 코스피와 대비된다. 코스피가 14.46% 급락한 10월 셋째주(12~16일)에도 삼양식품은 4.86% 오르며 강세를 보였다.

최고운 한국투자증권 연구원은 "최근 증시 혼란 속 방어주 역할이 기대되는 음식료업종에 대한 투자 관심이 되살아나는 것도 삼양식품의 재평가 타이밍을 앞당길 것"이라며 "저점 매수 기회라고 판단한다"고 평가했다.

원화 강세에도 견조한 해외 수요와 비용 관리가 실적 증가를 뒷받침할 것이란 분석이다. 최 연구원은 "글로벌 불닭 수요가 변함없이 좋았다"며 "2분기보다 마케팅 등 비용을 효율적으로 관리한 덕분에 환율 하락 영향을 만회했을 것"이라고 말했다.

다음달 발표 전망인 3분기 실적은 매출과 영업이익 모두 분기 최대 기록을 경신했을 것이란 분석이 나온다. 금융정보업체 에프앤가이드에 따르면 삼양식품의 3분기 연결 매출액과 영업이익 컨센서스(증권사 추정치 평균)는 각각 8178억원, 1865억원이다. 전년 동기보다 각각 29.4%, 42.5% 증가한 수치다. 예상대로라면 분기 매출은 처음으로 8000억원을 넘어서게 된다.

해외 판매망 확대가 실적 증가를 이끄는 요인으로 꼽힌다. 손현정 유안타증권 연구원은 "미국 주요 유통 채널 확대와 멕시코 신규 거래처 확보로 판매량 증가세가 지속되고, 중국은 중추절(추석) 및 광군제(유통가 연중 최대 쇼핑 행사) 선출고 수요가 반영될 것으로 예상한다"고 설명했다. 손 연구원은 3분기 삼양식품의 해외 매출이 전체 매출의 약 84%인 6782억원에 이를 것으로 내다봤다.

증권가가 주목하는 것은 내년 생산능력 확대다. 내년 1분기 가동 예정인 중국 자싱공장은 연간 11억3000만개의 생산능력을 갖춘다. 국내 공장에서 담당하던 중국 수출 물량을 현지 생산으로 전환하면 국내의 여유 생산능력을 상대적으로 판매단가가 높은 미국·유럽 물량에 배분할 수 있다. 밀양2공장 가동률 상승도 해외 판매량 증가를 뒷받침할 것으로 예상된다.

내년 중국 공장이 가동하면 국내 생산 여력을 미국과 유럽 판매 물량에 더 배분할 수 있을 전망이다. 한유정 한화투자증권 연구원은 "미국 판매량 비중은 2025년 17%에서 내년 25%로, 같은 기간 유럽 판매량 비중은 5%에서 12%로 높아질 것으로 전망한다"고 분석했다.

수요 증가에 대응하기 위한 추가 증설 필요성도 제기된다. 한 연구원은 "2029년 공급 부족 사태가 불가피하기에 연내 해외 신공장에 대한 의사결정이 이뤄질 것으로 예상한다"며 "중국 자싱 신공장 외 해외 신공장뿐만 아니라 중국 내 추가 공장 투자도 검토될 가능성이 높을 것으로 판단한다"고 밝혔다.

회사 측의 유럽 시장 브랜드 인지도를 높이기 위한 행보도 이어지고 있다. 김정수 삼양식품 회장은 지난 17일(현지시간) 프랑스 파리에서 열린 식품박람회 '시알 파리 2026'을 찾았다. 올해 처음 참가한 삼양식품은 불닭과 파스타 브랜드 '탱글'을 소개하고 시식 행사와 체험형 프로그램을 통해 현지 소비자 접점을 넓히고 있다.

이날 포털사이트 종목토론방에서는 "역시 삼비디아", "반도체 못 가면 삼양이 항상 잘나가지" 등 주가 흐름에 기대를 거는 개인투자자의 반응이 이어졌다.

김연지 기자는 한경닷컴 증권부에서 국내 주식시장과 상장사, 증권업계 및 금융투자상품을 취재하고 있습니다. 2023년부터 경제 분야를 취재해 왔으며, 기업 실적과 산업 변화, 시장 수급을 바탕으로 주가가 움직이는 배경을 짚는 기사를 씁니다. 퇴직연금 시장과 연금 투자 흐름을 분석하는 기획 시리즈 "연금 빌드업"도 연재하고 있습니다. 복잡한 금융시장과 투자 정보를 독자의 눈높이에서 풀어내고, 합리적인 투자 판단과 노후 자산 설계에 도움이 되는 인사이트를 전하는 기자가 되고자 합니다.

미국 중간선거가 치러지는 11월에는 주가 상승 탄력이 큰 기존 인기종목보다 저평가되고 현금흐름이 풍부한 종목에 주목해야 한다는 분석이 증권가에서 나왔다. 실적 전망치가 개선되는 종목 가운데 주가수익비율(PER)이 낮고, 증권사 목표주가 대비 상승여력이 크며 현금 창출력이 우수한 종목을 선별하는 전략을 펴야 한다는 조언이다.

22일 하나증권이 최근 10년 동안 11월의 글로벌 주식시장 성과를 분석한 결과에 따르면 미국 스탠더드앤드푸어스(S&P)500지수의 11월 평균 수익률은 4.1%로 12개월 중 가장 높았다. 10차례 중 9차례 상승해 승률도 90%에 달했다. 2000년 이후 중간선거가 치러진 6개 연도의 11월에도 S&P500지수는 평균 2.8% 상승했다. 같은 기간 나스닥100지수와 코스피지수의 평균 상승률은 각각 4.2%, 4.7%였다.

다만 미국의 중간선거가 치러진 해의 11월 성과를 뜯어보면 다른 해와 상승 종목군 구성에 차이가 있다고 이경수 하나증권 연구원은 지적했다. 중간선거가 없는 해의 11월에는 주가 변동성이 큰 고베타 종목과 거래대금 상위 종목, 실적 전망치가 상향된 종목이 상대적으로 강세를 보인 반면, 중간선거가 치러진 해에는 저평가된 알파(초과 수익 가능성이 있는) 종목이 높은 수익률을 기록했다는 것이다.

이경수 하나증권 연구원은 "비선거 시기에는 '호실적 유행주' 스타일이 강세"라며 "중간선거 해의 11월에는 주가수익비율(PER)이 낮고, 목표주가 괴리율이 큰 종목이 성과의 상위를 차지했다"고 분석했다.

그는 “약속의 11월이라도 중간선거 시기의 불확실성 및 보수성이 반영된 결과”라고 설명했다.

한경닷컴은 이 연구원의 분석을 토대로 금융정보업체 에프앤가이드의 데이터가이드 서비스를 활용해 국내 상장사 가운데 △최근 한 달간 12개 선행 PER 컨센서스(증권사 추정치 평균)가 20% 이상 하향됐고 △20일 종가가 목표주가 컨센서스까지 100% 이상 상승 여력이 있으며 △12개월 선행 주당순이익(EPS)이 하향되지 않은 15개 종목을 추렸다.

추려진 종목 중 12개월 선행 PER 하향 폭이 가장 큰 종목은 두산이다. 한 달 전 47.58배에서 27.84배로 41.5% 하락했다. 같은 기간 EPS 컨센서스는 19.3% 상향됐다. 20일 종가 101만원에서 목표주가 컨센서스인 226만4167원까지의 상승여력은 124.2%다. 두산은 전자사업 부문의 인공지능(AI) 서버와 반도체 패키지에 사용되는 동박적층판(CCL) 공급 확대에 따른 수혜가 기대되고 있다. DB증권도 CCL 공급 부족에 따른 가격 인상과 생산능력 확대를 근거로 두산의 목표주가를 180만원에서 200만원으로 상향한 바 있다.

SK하이닉스의 12개월 선행 PER은 4.38배에서 2.77배로 36.8% 낮아졌다. EPS 컨센서스는 4.2% 상향됐다. 20일 종가 122만3000원과 목표주가 컨센서스 325만7727원의 괴리율은 166.4%에 달한다.

한화엔진은 최근 한 달간 12개월 선행 PER이 15.81배에서 9.83배로 37.8% 하락했다. 같은 기간 EPS 컨센서스는 8.4% 상승했다. 20일 종가 3만4600원에서 목표주가 컨센서스인 8만636원까지 상승여력은 133.1%다. 기존 선박용 엔진에 더해 AI 데이터센터용 발전엔진이 새로운 성장동력으로 거론된다.

HD건설기계의 12개월 선행 PER도 한 달 전 10.2배에서 6.54배로 35.9% 낮아졌다. EPS 컨센서스는 0.1% 상향됐으며, 20일 종가 8만9700원에서 목표주가 컨센서스인 19만8167원까지의 상승여력은 120.9%다.

한경우 기자는 한경닷컴에서 주식투자에 대한 기사를 쓰고 있습니다. 개별 종목 분석과 퀀트 투자 콘텐츠에 특히 두각을 나타냅니다.

그는 2014년 농식품 전문 매체에서 기자 생활을 시작했고, 이후 경제매체 산업부로 자리를 옮겨 중화학공업과 해운, 제약·바이오 산업을 출입하며 주요 산업에 대한 이해를 쌓았습니다. 이를 바탕으로 심층적인 종목 분석 기사를 작성하고 있습니다.

‘한경우의 케이스스터디’ 코너에는 주로 퀀트 투자 콘텐츠가 연재되고 있습니다. 에프앤가이드와 코스콤의 데이터 플랫폼을 능숙하게 다루기에 특정 투자지표를 조건 삼아 관심을 가져 볼만한 종목을 선별해 독자들에게 제시합니다.

‘투자톡’ 코너를 통해서는 각 투자 전략을 장기간 시뮬레이션한 백테스트 콘텐츠를 선보이고 있습니다.

TechCrunch Founder Summit is a full-day gathering in Boston on November 4 where founders across all stages connect with top VCs and experienced entrepreneurs to gain tactical insights on building and scaling their companies. It’s the latest in our long line of founder-centric events, which are smaller and more hands-on than Disrupt.

For the founder looking to really get in the weeds during a one-day crash course, Founder Summit is the ideal place to get a head start on your 2027 plans for everything from hiring, establishing product market fit, finding investors, improving your leadership skills, and more.

All founders end up wrestling with the extensive, complicated mechanics of building a company from the ground up. There’s fundraising, hiring, legal, marketing, PR, and leadership, as well as the investors needing the means to vet, invest in, and develop founders as they build out their skills.

Founder Summit is the best way to cover all of the challenging questions with community members who have been there, and lived to tell the tale, through constructive failure and massive success.

The event takes place on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at the SoWa Power Station in Boston. It’s accessible via public transportation and a short walk from the Back Bay and Tufts Medical Center stops on the Orange Line, or the Broadway stop on the Red Line.

Then there’s Founder Summit week, taking place November 1-7. That’s when all of our Side Events are held , expanding the opportunities for you to gather with the community. And if you’re especially eager to take part, you can apply to host your own Side Event right here .

Pricing moves in phases, with our next increase happening after October 16. Our current pricing tiers are Investor for $399, Founder for $199, and students for $149 . items.title: Meta says Muse has over 10M users, with shopping a top activity
items.summary: Meta Muse users are adopting the app for shopping and personal productivity, the company said during Q3 earnings. The AI app now has over 10M users.
items.content:

Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW.

Meta said during its third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday that its AI app Muse has been adopted by more than 10 million users, confirming estimates released earlier this week by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.

But it is how people are using it, and how much they’re spending that has caught CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s attention. Zuckerberg said about 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily, helping improve retention.

He also shared that over a quarter of Muse’s engaged users who were shopping via the AI agent, had an average purchase size of over $200, which was surprising even to industry insiders.

“Plaid told us that they hadn’t seen activity like they’re seeing with their connector on any other service before,” Zuckerberg said, referring to the financial technology company that connects payment apps to customers’ bank accounts. Muse uses Plaid’s connector to enable agentic shopping.

Beyond shopping, Zuckerberg said other popular uses for Muse include personal productivity tasks, such as connecting the AI agent to users’ email or calendars. The exec stressed that this indicates users trusted Muse’s security setup, which includes a feature called “Muse Secure VM” designed to protect their data and privacy. He also mentioned that the forthcoming “Muse Confidential VM” will prevent even Meta from seeing users’ content.

Now that Muse has achieved “product-market fit,” Zuckerberg said Meta’s focus will shift to scaling the AI agent, increasing revenue, and optimizing its compute costs. Remarkably, the tech company is forecasting that Muse will eventually bring in more revenue per user than its “family of apps” users do today — meaning its users on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger. Currently, that figure is around “several hundreds of dollars annually,” Zuckerberg said.

Meta has said it ultimately intends to monetize Muse by keeping it free for most users, but keeping a percentage of the commerce taking place on the platform. Power users who want access to the most advanced AI models or more tokens will also have to pay.

Zuckerberg also noted that Meta believes Muse will be profitable after it scales.

“On the compute side, we are building out the capacity to serve more than a billion people over the next few years,” he told bankers and analysts on the Q3 earnings call. “In the near term, Muse is very compute-intensive to run, but we expect to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year, which will enable it to be profitable once the revenue lines are at scale.”

Muse will also play a central role in Meta’s smart glasses strategy. Reality Labs, the division responsible for smart glasses, VR, and the metaverse, is still losing billions. However, the division’s losses are expected to improve from $19.1 billion in 2025 to $15 billion this year.

Beyond scaling and supporting its hardware strategy, Zuckerberg teased the company’s plans for something he called the “Muse network.” He described this as taking Muse from a “single-player game” to one where “your Muses can work with your friends’ and your families’ [Muses].”

“And if you want to buy something, it’s not just navigating to that business’s website; it’s talking to their agent,” he added.

items.content:
Critical PHP Vulnerability (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) [infocon yellow]

Published : 2026-10-21. Last Updated : 2026-10-21 21:02:43 UTC

PHP.net announced that it will release a critical update today. We decided to change the infoCon to YELLOW due to the widespread use of PHP, the expected severity of the flaw (CVSS 9.4), and the availability of early PoC exploits before the patch became available.

Various vendors have released bulletins listing products that must be patched for this vulnerability. For example:

Cisco  https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-php-october26-Jj384Daq

OPNSense https://x.com/opnsense/status/2112985458514756087

PFSense https://forum.netgate.com/topic/201565/critical-php-security-update

Palo Alto Networks https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-109618

Many open source firewall/router products use PHP. Expect updates for them, and as always, do not expose the web admin interface to the internet.

PHP also published a summary around the release:

https://thephp.foundation/blog/2026/10/21/todays-php-security-release-and-how-were-strengthening-php-security/

The PHP update was released as scheduled: https://www.php.net/index.php#2026-10-20-1

This diary will be continuously updated today. I am starting to write this diary with many details still unclear and with the patch not yet available.

The easy answer: All of them. At least starting with PHP 5, including the most recent releases.

PHP Versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, all released today, are currently the only "safe" versions. Note that Linux distributions may backport the patch for older versions.

Ubuntu just released updated PHP packages for Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, 26.04, and  26.10. [ubuntu].

Only PHP 8 is expected to receive a patch. Older versions are no longer supported. The patch is expected to be released at 14:00 UTC today, October 21st. [php] Ubuntu will release patches "as soon as possible" and may include backported patches for PHP versions included in supported Ubuntu versions.

The real "race to patch" does not start at 14:00 UTC for most people, but at the time distributions release updated packages. Most PHP sites do not use PHP compiled from php.net directly. It will almost certainly be faster to wait for your distribution to release an update.

Does this vulnerability affect specific configurations or extensions?

The vulnerability is in the PHP core, and all default PHP installations are expected to be vulnerable (see below for mitigations).

What steps can I take to mitigate the vulnerability before applying the patch?

Early guidance suggests that the configuration setting " session.upload_progress.enabled = Off " provides partial mitigation against the vulnerability being exploited. By default, this setting is "On". Restricting the maximum allowed request size in your web server and/or PHP configuration may also help.

Are there WAF rules or other measures to protect a site running PHP?

Yes. I will add more as I verify them. Cloudflare appears to have already deployed some protections. Other vendors have likely done the same.

Cloudflare is reporting exploits [cloudflare]. PoC exploits and vulnerability details have been released [jackalsyn]

Wiz Security published a blog post detailing how they discovered the vulnerability using AI tools. [wiz]

This vulnerability is described as a remote code execution via out-of-memory corruption. [CVE-2026-109618]. The advisory describes several issues related to this vulnerability. Firstly, a multipart MIME request without a Content-Length header may bypass the post_max_size setting, which is intended to restrict the amount of data sent in a request. As a result, more data than expected may be sent to PHP. Second, the number of headers is not restricted, allowing for additional memory use. items.content:
Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates

Cisco Talos is aware of eight intermediate certificates belonging to the intermediate certificate authority, eMudhra . Rather than possessing the mandatory 384 bits of pseudo-random security, several private keys evaluated single-digit and double-digit integers. This misconfiguration allows an attacker with the private key of any of the compromised intermediate CAs to impersonate any website or service. Six of the TLS certificates, trusted by Chrome, Mozilla, and Apple have been blocked by these vendors already. Two other certificates, used for codesigning by Microsoft, have also been blocked. Talos expects there will be additional patches available across a variety of technologies as software applications work to remediate the certificates’ exposure.

Following the disclosure, eMudhra has revoked the compromised certificates and stopped issuing new certificates under its G3 root.

The cause of this issue, originated during an April 30, 2025 key generation activity conducted by eMudhra under its emSign Root TLS CA - G3 and cross-signed Comodo AAA Certificate Services.  During a key generation ceremony for 24 subordinate CAs, a flaw in eMudhra’s key generation process created a second set of weak P-384 keys during a wrap/unwrap step. Those keys were mistakenly used for eight intermediate CA certificates. This flaw took the encryption from 384 bytes of entropy down to 3 – 8, making recovering the private keys trivial. items.title: Lazarus hackers use post-quantum cryptography for malware delivery
items.summary: North Korean hackers are using a post-quantum cryptographic mechanism to secure malicious payload delivery in new operations that combine old and new malware. [...]
items.content:
Lazarus hackers use post-quantum cryptography for malware delivery

North Korean hackers are using a post-quantum cryptographic mechanism to secure malicious payload delivery in new operations that combine old and new malware.

The campaign targets South Korean organizations through a “rather complex” infection chain. Researchers at cybersecurity company Kaspersky dubbed the operation FlashHole and attributed it to the Lazarus Group.

Analysis of the malware revealed that the threat actor used the standardized ML-KEM post-quantum cryptographic mechanism to communicate with the command-and-control (C2) server for malware delivery.

Kaspersky says the attackers used LPEClient malware, previously associated with Lazarus , to receive ML-KEM-1024 public keys from its C2 infrastructure and generate shared keys that allowed it to decrypt subsequently incoming payloads.

According to the researchers, the attacks started in July 2025 and relied on phishing pages directing targets to specially crafted GitHub pages.

These pages load JavaScript code from external domains, triggering an in-memory execution chain that involved INISAFE CrossWeb EX, a security tool popular in South Korea.

The security tool’s process executed the legitimate Windows binary fsquirt.exe , which was used to run shellcode that installed TechHub, a downloader responsible for retrieving additional malware from private GitHub repositories.

Kaspersky identified at least three companies in South Korea, in the software, construction, and wired communication equipment manufacturing sectors, but suspects that many more organizations were affected.

Another new tool seen in these attacks is ClientHub, a loader that supports Dropbox communications as well as direct data exchange with LPEClient.

The researchers note that LPEClient profiles victims, receives encrypted payloads through ClientHub, and evades security monitoring.

Another malware observed in the attacks is Cubridge, a modular backdoor that provides file management, command execution, and reconnaissance capabilities, and also supports screenshot capturing and loading additional payloads on infected systems.

Kaspersky has also seen additional tools targeting Chromium-based browsers for account credentials, cookies, and browsing history.

The researchers note that most of Lazarus’ code runs in memory, though persistence mechanisms leave some files on the victim’s disk.

The use of the ML-KEM post-quantum cryptographic mechanism stands out in operation FlashHole since it is a NIST-approved standard present in  multiple software projects as a way to protect data from “ hack now decrypt later ” attacks.

The technical analysis showed that LPEClient obtained from the C2 "a byte array comprising four 1,568‑byte blocks," each containing an ML‑KEM‑1024 public key.

"LPEClient then generates four distinct pairs of shared keys and ciphertexts from these blocks, encrypts the ciphertexts with the GOST algorithm, and transmits them to the C2 server via ClientHub," Kaspersky explains.

The shared secrets supply the key material for Threefish, another encryption algorithm, which decrypts the response containing parameters and an executable payload.

The final payload is Cubridge, which LPEClient reflectively loads into the host’s memory.

Kaspersky believes Lazarus uses this method along with an in-memory execution chain to lower detection risk to a minimum.

“The use of post-quantum cryptography shows that the group intends to hide subsequent payloads," Kaspersky says.

Kaspersky researchers place FlashHole within the broader Cascade Hole activity and link it to the earlier Operation SyncHole with medium-to-high confidence.

items.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI
items.summary: Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model built largely by its own AI research system, as an early test of AI that improves itself.
items.content:
Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.

Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW.

Recursive , an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model, Flint , on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI.

Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months.

Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop.

The company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures. Recursive is led by CEO Richard Socher, Salesforce’s former chief scientist.

Because Flint runs on a user’s own computer rather than a company’s cloud servers, developers can use it offline, keep their code private, and avoid the usage fees that AI cloud services charge based on how much text the model processes. The model is free to download on Hugging Face, the popular site for sharing AI models, under the Apache 2.0 license, an open-source license that allows free use and modification.

Flint is a mixture-of-experts model, meaning it uses only a small slice of itself for any given task: just 2.5 billion of its 40 billion settings, known as parameters, at a time. That makes it light enough for an ordinary laptop and far smaller than Meta’s Muse Spark Open , an open model built for Macs that was released last week. Muse Spark Open uses 816 billion parameters and needs at least a terabyte of memory.

Flint is also fast. In Recursive’s tests, it generated about 131 tokens (chunks of text) per second on a MacBook Pro with Apple’s M4 Pro chip — roughly twice the 58 to 69 tokens per second that similar models managed on the same machine, including Google’s Gemma 4 and Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. On Nvidia’s RTX Spark, Flint topped 150 tokens per second.

On SWE-Bench Verified, a benchmark that measures how well AI can fix real-world software bugs, Flint outperformed other models under 50 billion parameters. On Recursive’s own average across six tests, only one model, Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 27B, scored higher than Flint.

The company acknowledged that Flint would need more guidance than the big paid coding assistants, and suggested breaking large tasks into smaller steps. Still, early reviews were positive.  Wired’s Will Knight used Flint on a Mac with 48GB of memory to build several small programs, including a to-do list app and a tool that scours the web for research. He found that smaller coding models often ran into errors or were slow compared to Claude or Codex, but Flint nailed his coding requests every time.

The Eureka Machine comes up with ideas, runs experiments and uses the results to decide what to try next. According to the company’s launch video , it contributed to nearly every part of building Flint, from pre-training to post-training and inference.

Recursive said that Eureka’s contributions include a sparser model shape, low-bit training that shrank Flint by 71% with almost no loss in quality and custom kernels, which are specialized programs that speed up the underlying computations.

Recursive didn’t say how much time the Eureka Machine saved its researchers, but it’s not alone in leaning on AI to do research. OpenAI said last month that by mid-August, its AI agents were logging 3.1 workdays…

The investment will support Peso’s expansion across four Latin American markets, where it connects stablecoin payments to merchant services and local banking networks.

Tether has led a pre-seed funding round in Bolivian fintech Peso, which offers USDT payments through food delivery apps and local banking networks, to support the company’s expansion across Latin America.

In a Wednesday announcement , Tether said the investment will help Peso expand its stablecoin payment infrastructure across Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Argentina, including services that connect USDT with local currencies through banking and merchant payment systems.

Peso has integrated USDT payments into Yango’s food delivery service in Bolivia, allowing customers to pay for orders using the stablecoin. The fintech offers QR payments, point-of-sale services for merchants and virtual accounts linked to Bolivia’s banking system through ACH transfers. Tether did not disclose the size of its investment.

The investment comes as other fintech companies expand USDT-based financial services in Bolivia. On Tuesday, lending platform Tala announced a partnership with El Dorado to offer credit directly through the digital wallet, allowing eligible customers to receive and repay loans in USDT on the Tempo blockchain.

Related: Tether, Kazakhstan cenbank mull tenge stablecoin and asset tokenization

Bolivia has increasingly turned to stablecoins since 2025 amid a prolonged US dollar shortage and high inflation, with businesses beginning to accept USDT for purchases as access to foreign currency became more difficult.

In November 2025, the government announced plans to integrate cryptocurrencies and stablecoins into the financial system, including allowing banks to offer digital asset custody and crypto-linked financial products.

The government subsequently began considering a regulatory framework in July 2026 that would recognize USDT for payments, savings and trade alongside the boliviano and US dollar.

The proposal came as Bolivia struggled with a prolonged dollar shortage after abandoning its longstanding currency peg in June, fueling demand for dollar-denominated alternatives such as USDT, as Cointelegraph reported in July.

items.title: Meta on the spot for $25 billion under New Mexico privacy ruling
items.summary: The Cambridge Analytica data privacy scandal from a decade ago is still weighing on Meta's finances.
items.content:
Image: Jay Openiano via Unsplash Meta on the spot for $25 billion under New Mexico privacy ruling

Meta must pay $25 billion in fines for data privacy violations related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal that became public almost 10 years ago, according to a New Mexico court filing released Wednesday.

In September, a jury found Meta had broken the state’s unfair practices law 43 million times for its role in the incident, which a whistleblower made public in 2018. Each violation carried civil penalties of as much as $5,000.

The state was initially awarded $220 billion, but state District Court Judge Francis Mathew reduced the penalty to $25 billion, according to the court filing. Meta will be charged 15% annual interest on the amount until the fine is paid off.

The case is tied to Meta-owned Facebook, which shared as many as 87 million users’ data with the Cambridge Analytica. The British political consulting firm then used the data to create psychological profiles of voters to facilitate targeted advertising, including in the 2016 presidential election.

New Mexico’s litigation focused on what Facebook told consumers about its data practices and how it combats misinformation and hate speech in the wake of the scandal becoming public, according to a press release from the office of Attorney General Raúl Torrez.

“The scale, duration, repetition, breadth, and willfulness of the violations, together with the evidence concerning Facebook's internal knowledge and practices … constitute substantial aggravating circumstances,” Mathew wrote in the filing.

Mathew highlighted the fact that senior Facebook leadership, including CEO Mark Zuckerberg and then-COO Sheryl Sandberg, created a calculated strategy to mislead consumers by among other things overseeing the creation of materials they called a “song sheet” to coordinate a public relations response.

“Facebook continued making public representations concerning users' control of data, third-party data misuse, misinformation, hate speech, and equal enforcement after employees, researchers, and senior personnel had internally identified that Facebook could not make good on its public promises,” the filing said, noting that Zuckerberg was aware of the deception.

The platform knew at the time that information regarding its data access infrastructure and enforcement protocols were not verifiable by users and the company took advantage of that, the filing said.

Facebook also failed to follow through on the “comprehensive” probe it promised consumers after the scandal became public, Mathew said.

The social media company was “aware at the time it made the promises that it did not have the ability to conduct such a thorough investigation or enforce deletion of the data due in large part to Facebook's poor record keeping and failure to vet third party developers at the time they were granted access to user data,” the filing said.

Pressure from senior leadership to minimize costs, a weak enforcement mechanism, poor investigative techniques and a focus on not setting a precedent for future probes caused Facebook to use an App Developer Investigation that was “willfully ineffective,” according to Mathew.

The ruling and Torrez’s approach to the enforcement “makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico,” Meta Chief Legal Officer C.J. Mahoney said in a statement.

“At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online.”

Meta plans to appeal the ruling, the statement said.

Torrez won $375 million in damages from Meta in March after a jury found the tech behemoth broke state law related to its kids’online safety practices.

Meta has already faced steep fines related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, including a $459 million penalty that was included in a roughly $17 billion August settlement with a group of several other state attorneys general pursuing the tech giant for its child safety practices.

items.summary: The US President detailed many schemes defrauding Americans, but referred only to “cybercurrency“ related to scams.
items.content:
The US President detailed many schemes defrauding Americans, but referred only to “cybercurrency“ related to scams.

US President Donald Trump hosted a roundtable at the White House on cybercrime, even as he and members of his administration face scrutiny from lawmakers and voters over accusations that they used their positions to enrich themselves with digital assets.

Speaking at the roundtable event on Wednesday, Trump said “countless” Americans lost more than $20 billion from cybercrime in 2025 through impersonation schemes, ransomware attacks, scam centers and other methods. The president added that federal officials had frozen $1 billion in “cybercurrency tied to foreign scammers” and prevented $1.6 billion in losses in 2025 from going to criminals engaging in cybercrime following a March executive order.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth (left), President Donald Trump (center) and Attorney General Todd Blanche (right) speaking at the White House on Wednesday. Source: White House

Notably, neither the president nor Attorney General Todd Blanche explicitly used the term “cryptocurrency” or “digital assets” when discussing the scams affecting many Americans, despite reports before the roundtable signaling a crackdown on foreign crypto scams would be the focus of the event. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin similarly only referred to “digital extortion.” “Cybercurrency,” the word Trump used, is a dated term for what many people now call cryptocurrency.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation reported that Americans had lost $11 billion from scams in 2025 specifically related to digital assets, including through crypto ATMs. Cointelegraph reached out to the White House for comment on the roundtable but did not receive an immediate response.

Related: Ex-Trump crypto adviser profited after helping pass stablecoin bill: WSJ

The president and his family are tied to several crypto ventures which Trump reported netted him $1.4 billion in 2025, while his alleged “schemes” cost investors about $4.7 billion , according to a Public Citizen report. His family’s crypto company, World Liberty Financial, also faces scrutiny for its USD1 stablecoin being used to settle a $2 billion investment in Binance by an entity tied to Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan in the United Arab Emirates.

Trump’s memecoin project, Official Trump (TRUMP), is hosting another dinner for tokenholders on Nov. 22. Similar events organized by the team behind the memecoin have prompted accusations from lawmakers and interest groups of Trump selling access to the presidency through “pay-to-play” schemes.

The White House roundtable followed reports that Italian authorities arrested 30 people for using crypto to launder millions of dollars through a bank allegedly tied to the mafia. According to Bloomberg, Italy’s police were investigating a criminal network that sent money from corporate fraud, crypto investment scams, and drug trafficking to digital wallets.

items.content:
OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Google's Gemini 4 Argon found critical PHP flaw affecting millions of websites

View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian

AI models from OpenAI and Google found a critical PHP vulnerability that could affect millions of websites worldwide.

GPT-5.6 Sol tracked down the flaw as part of the Patch-the-Planet initiative , which OpenAI calls one of the "most impactful security issues in recent memory." The model spotted the vulnerabilities before attackers did, giving developers and security vendors a window to respond. A tool on GitHub now lets server operators check whether their PHP version is affected.

Security firm Wiz found the same flaws independently, using its own Wiz Atlas platform alongside Google's Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol. Gemini 4 Argon proved especially useful for finding the vulnerability, developing exploits, building attack detection, and validating the patch, according to Wiz. Ad

An exploit that worked against one specific PHP installation used to require significant effort to adapt to other versions and configurations, Wiz explains. Large language models remove that barrier because they can automatically adjust exploits across different PHP versions, configurations, and memory layouts. "This significantly lowers the barrier to scaling attacks across different deployments," the firm writes, adding that "vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets." Ad

The fix was coordinated over two months across five phases, involving PHP developers, Wiz, Cloudflare, and US agencies including CISA and the White House. OpenAI is proposing this process as a repeatable framework for future AI-driven security discoveries.

The company expects findings on the scale of the PHP2Shell flaw to "increase sharply in the coming months," but warns that the same AI capabilities that find vulnerabilities can help attackers too. The discovery feeds into a months-long debate over AI models' offensive and defensive cybersecurity capabilities. Ad

items.title: Tech trio launches $10 million initiative to help under-resourced utilities bolster cybersecurity
items.summary: Up to 500 under-resourced utilities will receive support in order to bolster their cybersecurity through a private sector initiative launched this week.
items.content:
A water tower at the East Water Treatment Plant in Boynton Beach, Florida. Image: Quintin Soloviev / Wikimedia Commons Tech trio launches $10 million initiative to help under-resourced utilities bolster cybersecurity

Up to 500 under-resourced utilities will get access to a range of free cybersecurity software, hardware, deployment services and training through a new program offered by the global services company Accenture, the cybersecurity firm Dragos and the SANS Institute training organization.

The three organizations announced the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation on Tuesday, offering to provide eligible utilities with operational technology-focused cybersecurity services and more. They are collectively investing $10 million into the foundation.

The program is available to any U.S.-based water, wastewater, electric, and natural gas utilities with less than $100 million in annual revenue — which the companies said accounts for 97% of utilities.

Participants will get access to cybersecurity tools from Dragos, which notifies organizations of the devices on their network and ways they can address vulnerabilities.

Accenture will assist with deploying the tools and configuring them for participants. The company will also provide ongoing support for the utilities as they integrate the tools into their operations.

The SANS Institute will offer training to help build utilities’ employees capacity.

The initiative follows breaches of more than 100 water utilities across the U.S.. Government agencies continue to warn of both Chinese and Russian cyberattacks on energy utilties , telecoms and more .

Dragos CEO Robert Lee said cybercriminals and nation-states are “aggressively targeting utilities, attacking the operational environments that provide life-sustaining services to millions of Americans.”

The foundation “gives the utilities that need it most access to cybersecurity resources and training at no cost,” he added.

Members of the program will also have access to one another, allowing them to share best practices and operational experience.

“The best security technology in the world won’t protect a utility if its staff are not able to use it. The foundation puts training and skills in the hands of the people protecting the water, power, natural gas, and wastewater treatment systems that communities rely on,” said James Lyne, CEO of the SANS Institute.

The first phase of the program will involve 500 utilities and may expand depending on its success.

Cyber defenders have for years warned the public that most of the utilities in the U.S. cannot afford the cybersecurity tools needed to protect themselves against an array of evolving threats that include ransomware gangs, nation-state actors and other cybercriminals eager to cause damage.

Many utilities lack the funding, staffing and technological capacity to integrate cybersecurity tools — leaving thousands of pumps, valves, substations, and distribution networks vulnerable to attack.

There is no federal or state government involvement in the program. The cybersecurity company Elastic will also offer technical support to help scale the program.

There is no time limit on how long participants will have access to the program and Dragos said “other companies are already expressing interest in coming on board to grow it further.”

After the attacks on water utilities in July, the National Rural Water Association (NRWA) launched its own program involving five managed detection and response providers — Rapid7, Defendify, Legato Security, L1 Secure and Sentinel Technologies — who agreed to share threat information and data on vulnerability patches.

Federal efforts to improve the cybersecurity of utilities have stagnated, leaving states to create their own frameworks for protecting water, power, telecoms and more.

Walmart is embracing agentic commerce with the launch of its own Agent Gateway to manage transactions and other new features aimed at customers using AI agents, the retailer announced on Wednesday. The move comes shortly after Walmart’s top competitor, Amazon, began blocking AI agents from making purchases on behalf of online shoppers.

The company’s embrace of AI technology differentiates it from other online businesses, including not only Amazon but also various travel and booking sites, which have responded to the growing consumer adoption of AI agents by locking them out of their websites completely . Walmart, on the other hand, had already announced a partnership with a leading agent in the space, Meta’s Muse, and offers integrations with popular AI apps like ChatGPT, Gemini, and others.

Now, it’s expanding on those efforts with more technology to prepare for a world where AI agents become mainstream, said Walmart President and CEO John Furner, speaking at the Masters of Scale Summit in San Francisco on Wednesday. The technology will support agentic shopping from both Walmart and the company’s discount warehouse, Sam’s Club.

It starts with Walmart’s Agent Gateway, the company’s new MCP server, which is designed to help approved agents connect to Walmart over the model context protocol (MCP). The protocol, originally created by Anthropic, allows AI agents to connect to external data sources, tools, and other workflows. In this case, it lets an AI agent search across Walmart’s online inventory and make purchases on behalf of the agent’s user.

What’s more, the retailer says that its Agent Gateway will be able to help customers shop for their usual brands or items without having to share their personal information or purchase history directly with the agent.

The company has also developed new technology to differentiate an agent’s purchases from those initiated directly by the customer, and to give shoppers more control over what their agents can and cannot do.

With Agent Profiles, rolling out next month, customers will be able to authorize each AI agent they use with a dedicated profile in their account, allowing them to see the agent’s purchases separately from their own. Plus, customers will be in control of how purchases get approved by either requiring approval for each transaction or by authorizing transactions within a certain spending limit they set.

The retailer says these controls are similar to adding someone as an authorized user on your credit card, where their transactions are identified, and you can cap their spending.

The Agent Profiles will be created the first time you use a given agent to shop through the Walmart Agent Gateway, the company notes. To get started, you’ll authorize and link the Agent Profile to your Walmart account, then set your controls or spending limits. You can also delete an Agent Profile at any time. Agent support is available for anyone with a Walmart account; a Walmart+ membership is not necessary.

Alongside these technologies, Walmart is introducing special “terms” for AI agents, which specify how they must operate and what rights they have to transact on its site. Of note, Walmart says that its returns process applies, including when an agent doesn’t act as intended. That’s a customer-friendly condition that could sway consumers who were worried about being an early tester of agentic commerce, as they won’t fear ending up with products they don’t want because of a misbehaving agent.

Walmart also says that agents can’t take actions beyond what the shopper intends, can’t access the customers’ payment information, and can only access the information they need for the given task. Agents that don’t comply with the terms will be blocked from accessing Walmart’s site.

items.title: Critical GitLab Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Could Allow Unauthenticated RCE Across 12 Years of Releases
items.summary: GitLab released fixes on October 21 for a flaw that lets an attacker run code on a self-managed server without logging in, and it affects every version of the software going back to 7.0, released in 2014. The fix matters even for administrators who patched nine days earlier: the
items.content:
GitLab released fixes on October 21 for a flaw that lets an attacker run code on a self-managed server without logging in, and it affects every version of the software going back to 7.0, released in 2014.

The fix matters even for administrators who patched nine days earlier: the October 12 update covered only versions 19.2 and later, and the new fixed versions sit one patch above it, so an instance updated then is in range again.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-110264 , is rated 10.0 on the CVSS scale, the maximum. GitLab says that, under certain conditions, it could allow an unauthenticated user to run arbitrary code on the server due to an integer overflow during the compilation of a specially crafted regular expression.

GitLab has not said what those conditions are. The company reports no sign the flaw has been used in attacks, and it is not listed in the U.S. CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities as of October 22.

Only self-managed installations need to act. GitLab.com already runs the fixed version, and GitLab Dedicated tenants on the internal releases 19.3.5-internal0 and 19.4.2-internal0 or later already have the fix.

GitLab fixed the flaw in seven versions at once.

The table below pairs each release branch with the version that fixes it.

Four of those versions are older than GitLab normally patches. The company's policy covers the current release and the previous two monthly releases, which, as of today, are 19.5, 19.4, and 19.3.

GitLab said it backported this fix to 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, and 19.2.9 on top of its standard releases, a step it reserves for severe issues.

The reason the flaw reaches so far back is the part of GitLab that failed. The regular-expression compiler is Ruby's built-in engine, called Onigmo, which GitLab ships inside its own packages and patches in its own builds. A weakness in that engine is present wherever GitLab has shipped it, which is every release since 7.0.

GitLab also published two detection rules to help self-managed administrators look for exploitation attempts, named "Onigmo native worker crash" and "Org mode render error burst." They are part of the company's open-source TLDR framework , which writes each detection in the Sigma format against GitLab's own application logs.

GitLab has not said what preconditions an attacker needs to reach the compiler, so administrators cannot yet rule themselves out by configuration; the fix is the only certain protection, and GitLab's advisory offers no interim workaround.

This is the fourth code-execution flaw in GitLab's regular-expression engine that the same researcher, who uses the handle joaxcar, has reported in a month, and the first to reach versions before 19.2.

On October 12 , GitLab fixed CVE-2026-97229, also an unauthenticated 10.0 overflow in the regex compiler, in versions 19.2.8, 19.3.5, and 19.4.2. On September 23 , it fixed two more, CVE-2026-93577 and CVE-2026-89078, both rated 9.9 but requiring a logged-in account. The three earlier flaws stopped at version 19.2; this one does not.

The October 21 release fixes 11 security issues in all, one critical and the rest high, medium, or low.

Two of the others concern authentication. CVE-2026-15723, rated high at 8.2, could allow a logged-in user to take over another account, but only when an administrator has enabled both SAML and LDAP auto-linking.

A cache-poisoning flaw in GitLab's OAuth and OpenID Connect endpoints, CVE-2026-112212, rated high at 7.5, could allow an attacker to redirect certain sign-in flows to a server they control in setups that use a shared cache.

The upgrade carries a cost worth planning for. The 19.4.3 and 19.3.6 releases include database changes that run during the upgrade, and on a single-node server that means downtime while they finish. GitLab says multi-node setups can apply the patch without downtime using its zero-downtime procedure.

items.content:
CISA: Hackers chain Plex flaws in Plex2Shell attacks to breach servers

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) is warning that attackers are actively exploiting four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server.

The security issues are collectively called Plex2Shell. When chained in an exploit, an attacker can obtain the owner's admin token and execute code with elevated privileges.

Plex Media Server is a popular media suite that helps users organize personal collections of movies, TV shows, music, and photos, and stream them to other devices at home or remotely over the internet.

CISA has directed federal agencies to prioritize patching systems affected by Plex2Shell vulnerabilities or apply mitigations by October 23.

The security issues were discovered by security researcher Zach Main, who reported them responsibly to Plex on July 27.

The individual flaws are rated medium to high in severity, but the researcher assigns the full exploit chain a critical score of 9.8.

CVE-2026-96652 – An SSRF flaw in /player/timeline that allows unauthenticated attackers to make Plex send POST requests to arbitrary destinations, including its own internal APIs.

CVE-2026-96654 – A URL injection flaw in searchOne that allows attackers to invoke other plugins’ functions with attacker-controlled parameters.

CVE-2026-96655 – An authenticated SSRF flaw in the transcoder endpoint that allows users to make Plex request arbitrary internal or external addresses.

CVE-2026-96656 – An arbitrary file write flaw in the transcoder settings that allows administrators to plant malicious shared libraries that Plex subsequently loads, leading to code execution.

Zach Main published full technical details for the Plex2Shell vulnerabilities on October 16, followed by a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit three days later.

On October 17, reports of Plex2Shell being exploited in the wild started to emerge, intially targeting  Plex honeypots to deploy a cryptominer.

Plex2Shell impacts Plex Media Server versions before 1.43.3.10861, which was released on August 4 .

Hackers also target Siemens Software Center

Alongside Plex2Shell, CISA has added to its catalog of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities ( KEV ) an uncontrolled search path element flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-110936, in Siemens Software Center (SSC).

The German technology giant  warned on October 19  that hackers were leveraging the vulnerability in campaigns linked to a multi-payload ClickFix delivery platform called Romulus.

Recent research from operational technology (OT) cybersecurity company Forescout notes that Romulus "may be a privately operated panel, a commercial cybercriminal delivery service, an affiliate framework, or software that has been copied between operators."

Siemens's alert on CVE-2026-110936 shares indicators of compromise (IoCs) and advice on identifying compromised systems, urging administrators to update Siemens Software Center to version 4.0.9.8 or later.

CISA has also added CVE-2026-106931 to KEV, an OS command injection flaw that affects affecting the SiteGuard Server Edition web application firewall (WAF).

Both the vendor and Japan's CERT flagged CVE-2026-106931 as actively exploited late last week.

The vendor urged users to upgrade to SiteGuard Server Edition for Apache httpd, Nginx, and IIS version 8.00 Update 5, and SiteGuard Server Edition for Apache httpd and Nginx on FreeBSD version 7.00 Update 6 and later.

items.summary: The pair stressed the latest update showed no country is pursuing the technically challenging effort to interfere with or hack into the country’s election infrastructure or tamper directly with votes.
items.content:
Image: Laurie Shall / Wikimedia Commons Democrat lawmakers say Russia is aiming to undermine party ahead of midterms

The Russian government is attempting to harm the Democratic Party and erode voter confidence ahead of the upcoming midterm elections, continuing a decade-long trend, according to two senior congressional lawmakers.

A classified U.S. intelligence community assessment, which was shared with Congress in recent days, also found China is again engaging in targeted influence efforts, as are other foreign powers like Iran and North Korea, according to Rep. Jim Himes (CT), the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee.

“The Russians are kind of throwing everything out there — chaos, don't trust your institutions, voting machines,” he told reporters on Wednesday during a roundtable discussion on Capitol Hill. “They're throwing everything out there to generate a sense of chaos and anarchy.”

Mark Warner (D-VA), the vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, noted that “every election cycle since 2016, Russia has spread disinformation” to undermine Democrats. “That’s just a factual basis.”

Both lawmakers hedged at how explicit the Kremlin’s actions have been, though they suggested that U.S. support for Ukraine is being used as a wedge issue, similar to the 2022 midterms . The pair stressed the latest update showed no country is pursuing the technically challenging effort to interfere with or hack into the country’s election infrastructure or tamper directly with votes.

“Nothing out there suggests that there is either the capability or the intent to do interference, whereas there is a pretty robust influence environment,” Himes said.

The findings come amid rising concerns from Democrats at the state and federal level that President Donald Trump will seek to exploit misinformation and conspiracy theories before, during and after Election Day. Republicans are expected to take losses in key races and potentially lose control of both chambers of Congress to Democrats.

Such fears have persisted ever since Trump refused to accept his loss in the 2020 presidential election. Upon returning to the Oval Office, he warned that the country’s election systems are vulnerable to foreign meddling, sent federal agents to scour state voter rolls and installed election deniers in Cabinet-level positions.

The longstanding and increasingly aggressive attacks on voting systems have many election officials and Democrats afraid that the administration is laying the groundwork to challenge the election’s validity in November.

“We are making the assumption that all the stops will be pulled out,” Himes told reporters.

To that end, the two lawmakers are assuming Trump will not accept the election’s results if it is not in his favor, and have wargamed a variety of scenarios, including the president seizing on an isolated, or possibly fabricated, piece of intelligence to blocking the seating of the new Congress in January.

In addition, Warner and Himes said they have sought assurances from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and CIA Director John Ratcliffe to be available on Election Day if the commander-in-chief makes unsubstantiated claims on social media or elsewhere.

While such possible conversations might involve classified information, Himes noted, he could at least go on television to say there has been no briefing or information to suggest the accusations are accurate.

“Now, does that end the crisis? No, but that's the first step.”

The Connecticut lawmaker said his panel would receive another election security briefing next week, one arranged by panel chairman Rick Crawford (R-AR).

Warner said his committee would push for a similar closed-door session.

items.title: NVIDIA Kumo Relational Outperforms Supervised Machine Learning on Relational Data, No Training Required
items.content:
NVIDIA Kumo Relational is a pre-trained relational foundation model that makes predictions directly on enterprise databases. Given a predictive query, it gathers up to 10,000 historical examples as context and predicts outcomes such as churn, demand, or fraud in a single forward pass. It needs no task-specific training, no feature engineering, and no flattening of tables. Kumo Relational is the first few-shot foundation model to outperform supervised machine learning on common relational benchmarks. Across 41 tasks on 15 databases, it beats supervised relational deep learning models and expert-engineered gradient-boosted tree pipelines, and on the SAP SALT enterprise benchmark it surpasses AutoGluon ensembles by 8% in mean reciprocal rank (MRR). It scales to databases with 500B+ rows and works for humans and agents alike, through NVIDIA's open-source, GPU-native structured-data-models library or as an NVIDIA NIM.

Foundation models have already rewritten the playbook for language and vision. Not long ago, production NLP meant a dedicated model per task, each fed by its own pipeline of tokenization, lemmatization, and n-grams. LLMs made that stack largely obsolete for three reasons: they were more accurate than the best task-specific models, far simpler to put into production, and flexible enough to open a new era of agentic applications.

The same shift is now underway for structured data. Relational databases power the world's most critical business decisions, yet predictive modeling on them still requires weeks of feature engineering, task-specific training, and tuned pipelines. Structured data foundation models change that for the same three reasons:

Better accuracy today: As drop-in replacements, these models already beat many production pipelines, especially XGBoost. On RelBench V1 classification tasks, Kumo Relational outperforms gradient-boosted trees on expert-engineered features by nearly 4 AUROC points on average. On SAP SALT, it beats XGBoost on engineered features by 7 MRR points out of the box and by 13 MRR points after fine-tuning. These results make a compelling case for replacing production XGBoost pipelines with Kumo Relational.

Simplicity and agility: One pre-trained model replaces separate pipelines for individual tasks. A new prediction becomes a query instead of a project, so ML teams can finally take on use cases that traditional ML made too laborious to build at every level of the organization.

Agents that can predict: LLMs let agents read, write, and reason. Structured data foundation models let them anticipate what happens next, such as which customer will churn, and act on it. Kumo Relational is already built to be called by agents, and its Predictive Query Language (PQL) gives them a simple interface for asking predictive questions.

Today, we are introducing Kumo Relational ( paper , documentation ), a pre-trained foundation model that brings this paradigm to relational data. Connect a database, describe what to predict, and get predictions in a single forward pass. No training required.

Most foundation models for structured data operate on a single flat table. Real-world data lives in relational databases instead: users connected to orders connected to products, all evolving over time. Flattening these relationships into one row through manual aggregation ( e.g. , "average order value in the last 30 days") loses fine-grained structural signals and takes significant human effort.

Kumo Relational is a Relational Foundation Model that operates directly on the database, respecting its tables, foreign keys, and timestamps. It is pre-trained once on synthetic relational data that reflects real-world datasets and adapts to each new task through in-context learning , reading up to 10,000 context examples at inference time. Each example pairs a local subgraph around an entity at a point in time with its ground-truth target ( e.g. , "this user churned" or "this item sold 142 units").
