items.summary: The popular LiteLLM Python package has been compromised as part of a software supply chain attack that delivered a credential stealer and a backdoor, according to reports from SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity, and Upwind. The compromise affects LiteLLM 1.107.0, distributed through P
items.content:
The popular LiteLLM Python package has been compromised as part of a software supply chain attack that delivered a credential stealer and a backdoor, according to reports from SafeDep , Socket , StepSecurity , and Upwind .

The compromise affects LiteLLM 1.107.0, distributed through PyPI wheels and Docker images. The Python package has since been quarantined on Python Package Index (PyPI), and the malicious Docker images have been removed.

Oliver Jensen, director of security at LiteLLM, said an investigation into the incident is ongoing, and that it's still working to trace the original attack vector by which the threat actor published the malicious release.

"We have identified that the malicious actions were taken through three engineers' GitHub accounts, appearing to be by way of stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens," Jensen said . "The threat actor used one user's account to trigger the project-releaser run, and another user's account to approve it. All tokens which were involved in this attack have been revoked."

"We have not yet identified the mechanism by which the threat actor acquired the relevant tokens, so cannot yet assert that no further access to these GitHub accounts. As a temporary mitigation, we have removed all but one (unaffected) user from our GitHub organization."

Separately, LiteLLM said it has updated the public registries to remove any trusted links to its GitHub organization so as to prevent further publication of malicious packages.

Analysis of the malicious version shows that it's equipped to collect cloud credentials, private keys, browser data, and authentication files for AI development tools. The following wheels are affected -

"The first payload is a credential stealer that calls itself privcollect," StepSecurity said. "The second payload forks a background daemon that checks a GitHub dead drop every hour and runs whatever Python the attacker serves."

The malware is launched by Python even before LiteLLM is imported through a path file ("cook.pth"), which is designed to automatically execute code when the interpreter starts. It's worth noting that the same behavior was observed in the LiteLLM compromise that took place as part of the TeamPCP supply chain attacks earlier this March .

The "cook.pth" file contains a single line, "import cook," which, in turn, launches the credential collector payload. This includes harvesting cloud tokens, developer accounts and private keys, AI tooling credential JSON files, browser data associated with Chromium and Firefox, and environment variables.

The malware is also capable of targeting LiteLLM deployments with an aim to extract the proxy's saved credentials and model configuration. The collected data is packaged into a GZIP-compressed TAR archive and sent to "litellm[.]dev/healthcheck" by means of an HTTP POST request.

In addition, the malware is designed to read the contents of a text file ("domain.txt") located within a GitHub repository ("github[.]com/letters9813"), check if it holds a domain and, if so, run the same stealer, and finally run an HTTP GET request against "<domain>/codepy" and execute the response. The GitHub repository currently returns a 404 error.

Users who have downloaded the malicious version are advised to revoke and replace exposed credentials from a clean environment and pin version 1.106.2 by digest.

items.content:
오픈AI가 '챗GPT'의 개인정보 보호 기능을 강화하고 민감한 대화에 대한 접근을 제한하는 새로운 기능을 선보였다. 대화 기록과 메모리를 일반 채팅과 분리해 사적인 정보가 노출될 가능성을 줄이는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

오픈AI는 20일(현지시간) 챗GPT에서 민감한 대화를 별도로 보호할 수 있는 '채팅 잠금(Locked Chats)' 기능을 도입했다.

사용자가 다른 사람에게 기기를 보여주거나 화면을 공유할 때 사적인 대화가 노출되는 것을 막기 위한 기능이다.

잠금 기능을 적용한 대화는 일반 채팅 기록과 검색 결과에서 사라지고, 별도의 '잠긴 채팅(Locked chats)' 섹션에 보관된다. 웹과 데스크톱에서는 4자리 PIN으로 잠금을 해제할 수 있으며, 지원되는 모바일 기기에서는 페이스ID와 터치ID, 기기 잠금 해제 방식도 사용할 수 있다.

일반적인 대화 기록과 메모리 기능도 분리된다. 메모리 기능이 활성화되면 잠긴 대화에서 새로 입력한 정보는 잠긴 채팅끼리 공유되는 별도 메모리에 반영되며, 일반 대화의 메모리에는 업데이트되지 않는다. 다만 잠금 설정 이전에 챗GPT가 이미 기억한 정보까지 삭제되는 것은 아니다.

Keep sensitive conversations out of view with Locked Chats in ChatGPT.

Move chats out of your regular history and search into a protected space you can unlock with a PIN on web and desktop, or a PIN, Face ID, Touch ID, or device unlock on supported mobile devices.

New messages… pic.twitter.com/tV0wBj8f0i

이번 기능은 일시적인 대화(Temporary Chat)와 달리 대화를 기록으로 남겨두면서 접근을 제한하는 방식이다. 일시적인 대화는 일반 기록에 저장되지 않지만, 잠긴 채팅은 사용자가 언제든 다시 열어 이어갈 수 있다.

다만 채팅 잠금이 종단간 암호화나 별도의 암호화 저장소를 제공하는 것은 아니다. 대화 보관 기간이나 모델 개선 설정도 바뀌지 않는다. 따라서 민감한 대화에 대한 접근을 제한하는 기능이지, 저장된 데이터의 처리 방식 자체를 변경하는 보안 기능은 아니다.

PIN을 재설정할 때는 주의가 필요하다. 기존 PIN을 재설정하면 잠긴 대화와 해당 대화에만 저장된 기억, 보호된 파일 등이 영구 삭제되며 복구할 수 없다. 잠긴 대화는 그룹 채팅과 보관된 대화, 일시적인 대화, 예약 작업이나 회의 녹음이 연결된 대화 등 일부 유형에서는 사용할 수 없다.

오픈AI는 이번 기능을 무료 요금제와 고, 플러스, 프로, 비즈니스, 엔터프라이즈, 에듀 사용자에게 차례로 배포하기 시작했다. 다만 헬스케어용 챗GPT에서는 제공되지 않는다.

items.title: Cardano Foundation urges EU against expanding MiCA rules to DeFi and staking
items.summary: The foundation called for regulation based on financial risks rather than technology, warning that overlapping rules could create uncertainty for crypto businesses across the EU.
items.content:
The foundation called for regulation based on financial risks rather than technology, warning that overlapping rules could create uncertainty for crypto businesses across the EU.

The Cardano Foundation has urged the European Union not to introduce new, standalone regulations for decentralized finance and staking, arguing that existing financial laws should govern such activities based on their functions and risks rather than the technologies they use.

In a Wednesday blog post outlining its 19-page Sept. 30 submission to the European Commission, the foundation called for a distinction between direct participation in decentralized networks and financial services provided by intermediaries, particularly those involving custody or control of users’ assets.

“Regulation should follow the substance of an activity, the functions performed, and the risks created, not the technology through which it is conducted,” the foundation wrote.

The foundation said Cardano users can delegate their native ADA (ADA) tokens to help secure the network without surrendering custody or locking their tokens, arguing that such participation should be treated differently from staking services operated by intermediaries.

The submission also called for clearer distinctions between the EU’s Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation (MiCA) and existing financial laws, warning that overlapping requirements and inconsistent interpretations across member states could create uncertainty for crypto businesses.

The foundation’s position comes as EU regulators consider expanding oversight of crypto services. In September, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) recommended additional safeguards for staking, lending and borrowing, along with a new regulated service category for firms providing access to DeFi protocols.

The Cardano Foundation has also pushed for greater regulatory clarity across the Atlantic, joining five other blockchain organizations in an Oct. 20 letter urging the US Securities and Exchange Commission to formally recognize digital commodities as non-securities under its proposed crypto framework.

items.content:
광양시육아종합지원센터에서 유아와 보호자를 위한 가족 문화공연 ‘샌드매직쇼’가 열렸다.

광양은 지난 17일 육아종합지원센터 대강당에서 유아와 보호자 등 200여명이 참여한 가운데 공연을 2차례 진행했다고 21일 밝혔다.

프로그램은 샌드아트와 코믹 키즈 매직쇼로 구성됐다. 샌드아트 공연에서는 동화 ‘아낌없이 주는 나무’를 모래 그림과 캐릭터로 표현했다.

이어진 마술공연에서는 어린이 참여형 마술과 공중부양 마술, 풍선 퍼포먼스 등을 선보였다. 일부 어린이들은 직접 무대에 올라 공연에 참여했다.

광양시육아종합지원센터는 올해 5월과 10월 두 차례 가족 문화공연을 운영했으며, 오는 11월과 12월에도 각각 한 차례씩 추가 공연을 진행할 예정이다.

광양시육아종합지원센터 관계자는 “앞으로도 영유아와 가족이 일상에서 문화예술을 접할 수 있도록 공연과 체험 프로그램을 지속적으로 운영하겠다”며 “아이들의 건강한 성장과 가족의 행복을 지원하는 데 힘쓰겠다”고 말했다.

items.content:
광주에서 도시농업을 직접 체험할 수 있는 ‘2026 광주 도시농부 축제’가 열린다.

전남광주통합특별시는 오는 23일부터 25일까지 광주청사 잔디광장 일원에서 ‘누구나 시작하는 도시농업…오늘, 도시에서 농부할래?’를 주제로 축제를 개최한다고 21일 밝혔다.

행사에는 한국원예치료복지협회 광주특별시지회를 비롯해 마스터가드너, 치유농업협회, 청년농업인 단체, 지역대학과 관련 기관·단체 등이 참여한다.

행사장에서는 도시농업 홍보 전시와 함께 반려식물 만들기, 허브미스트 만들기, 손수건 염색 등 체험 프로그램을 운영한다.

도시농업 전문가와의 1대1 맞춤교육을 통해 텃밭과 식물 관리 등 일상에서 활용할 수 있는 도시농업 정보도 제공한다.

어린이집을 대상으로는 상추 화분을 직접 만드는 ‘어린이 도시농부학교’를 운영한다. 지역대학과 연계한 기후위기 체험과 중앙아시아 다문화가정 프리마켓, 헤나 염색 체험도 마련된다.

24일과 25일에는 도시농업의 치유기능과 텃밭정원 치유 프로그램, 도시농업의 미래, 도시농업형 치유정원 등을 주제로 세미나가 진행된다. 도시농부들의 농악놀이와 추수감사 음악회 등 공연 프로그램도 운영한다.

배귀숙 도시농업과장은 “이번 축제는 도시텃밭을 비롯해 치유농업, 반려식물 등 도시농업의 다양한 영역을 아우르는 체험과 전시, 세미나 등을 준비했다”며 “시민들이 축제에서 농업의 가치와 지속가능한 환경의 중요성, 지역 공동체 간 화합을 느끼는 계기가 되길 바란다”고 말했다.

items.content:
AI 모델 경쟁이 성능뿐 아니라 응답 속도와 비용 효율성으로 확대되는 가운데, 확산 대형언어모델(dLLM)이 기존 모델의 한계를 넘어설 수 있다는 가능성을 보여주는 사례가 등장했다. 초고속 생성 능력에 더해 오픈AI와 앤트로픽의 모델에 버금가는 성능을 입증하며 복잡한 AI 에이전트 작업까지 겨냥했다.

인셉션(Inception)은 19일(현지시간) 초당 1000토큰 이상을 생성하면서도 'GPT-6 루나'와 '클로드 하이쿠 5.5'보다 높은 품질을 내세운 dLLM '머큐리 3(Mercury 3)'를 출시했다. 모델 규모를 이전 세대보다 40배 이상 키우고도 빠른 속도를 유지한 것이 특징이다.

"지금까지 출시된 dLLM 가운데 가장 강력하고 지능적인 모델"이라고 소개했다. 자체 벤치마크 결과를 기준으로 GPT-6 루나와 하이쿠 5.5보다 높은 품질을 보이면서 초당 1000토큰 이상의 생성 속도를 구현했다는 설명이다. 엔비디아 GPU 환경에서 측정한 생성 속도는 초당 1068토큰이다.

핵심 기술은 텍스트를 차례로 생성하는 대신 여러 위치의 토큰을 병렬로 다듬는 확산 방식이다. 기존 자기회귀(autoregressive) 모델은 앞선 토큰이 생성돼야 다음 토큰을 만들 수 있지만, 확산 모델(diffusion model)은 전체 답변의 초안을 만든 뒤 여러 단계에 걸쳐 동시에 개선한다. 순차 처리 단계를 줄여 응답 지연을 낮출 수 있다.

머큐리 3가 확산 모델도 규모를 키우면 지능을 높일 수 있다는 점을 보여준다고 강조했다. 첫 번째 모델인 '머큐리 1 미니'보다 전체 매개변수 규모를 40배 이상 늘렸으며, 두 모델 간 표준 벤치마크 평균 성능은 약 3배 향상됐다고 밝혔다. 다만 구체적인 매개변수 수는 공개하지 않았다.

이번 출시가 AI 성능을 높이면서도 지연 시간과 비용 부담을 줄일 수 있는 새로운 방법이라고 강조했다. "확산 모델은 지능이 비례적인 지연 시간 증가 없이 성장할 수 있는 새로운 길을 연다"고 밝혔다.

자체 벤치마크에서는 코딩과 지시 이행 분야에서 강점을 보였다. 'SWE-벤치 아틀라스' 점수는 51.08로, GPT-6 루나의 33.33과 하이쿠 5.5의 32.26을 웃돌았다. 'IF벤치'에서도 76.84점을 기록해 GPT-6 루나보다 약 15점 높았다. 'GPQA 다이아몬드' 점수는 89.23이었다.

모든 항목에서 경쟁 모델을 앞선 것은 아니다. '딥SWE v1'에서는 하이쿠 5.5가 51.62점으로 머큐리 3의 46.31점을 앞섰다. 긴 문맥에서 정보를 검색하는 'MRCR v2'에서도 하이쿠 5.5가 우위를 보였다. 일부 장문 검색과 복잡한 코딩 작업에서는 개선 여지가 남아 있는 셈이다.

머큐리 3는 코드 리뷰와 대화형 교육, 웹 탐색, 실시간 검색, 고객 지원 등 응답 속도가 중요한 AI 에이전트에 활용할 수 있다. 에이전트는 작업을 수행하는 과정에서 모델에 여러 차례 요청을 보내기 때문에 단계별 지연이 누적되기 쉽다. 빠른 응답을 제공하면 웹 탐색이나 문서 분석을 더 신속하게 진행하고, 제한된 시간 안에 여러 접근 방식을 시도할 수 있다는 설명이다.

얼리 액세스 파트너들도 다양한 활용 사례를 제시했다. 웹 탐색 자동화 업체 타이니피시(TinyFish)는 실제 웹 탐색 작업 50건 가운데 머큐리 3가 50%를 완료했다고 밝혔다. 옥텐 AI(Octen AI)는 스마트 안경 기반 검색에서 중앙값 기준 생성 시간이 0.9초, 전체 응답 시간이 2.2초였다고 전했다. 리비전두조(RevisionDojo)는 학습용 힌트와 답안 표시 기능이 약 1초 만에 제공된다고 설명했다.

이 모델은 인셉션 API 플랫폼과 오픈라우터, 베이스텐, 버셀 등을 통해 이용할 수 있다. 오픈AI API와 호환돼 기존 개발 환경에 비교적 쉽게 통합할 수 있으며, 최대 100만 토큰의 문맥 길이를 지원한다.

정식 가격은 입력 토큰 100만개당 0.20달러, 출력 토큰 100만개당 0.70달러다. 출시 기념으로 50% 할인된 입력 0.10달러, 출력 0.35달러에 제공하며, 캐시된 입력 토큰은 입력 가격에서 90% 할인한다. 기업용 고객에게는 전용 처리 용량과 자동 확장, 데이터 보존 설정 등 추가 기능도 지원한다.

인셉션은 음성 AI의 첫 응답 지연을 줄이는 '머큐리 보이스(Mercury Voice)'와 대량 분류 작업에 특화한 의사결정 모델 '머큐리 디사이드(Mercury Decide)'도 함께 선보이며 실시간 AI 제품군을 확대하고 있다.

items.content:
Google Cloud now offers OpenAI models alongside Gemini and Claude, becoming the only major provider with all three

View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian

Google Cloud is now the only major cloud provider offering Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI models on one platform. Three OpenAI models are available starting today : GPT-6 Astra for demanding tasks like coding and research, GPT-6.1 Sol as a cheaper alternative with similar performance, and GPT-6 Luna as a fast, cost-efficient option for everyday use.

The models launch as a private preview for select enterprise customers, with sign-ups open now . They'll also appear in Gemini for Business and Google Antigravity. All charges run through a single Google Cloud bill and count toward existing contracts. Google says customer data won't be used for training.

The move highlights a recurring tension at Google: compute capacity spent serving cloud customers strengthens the biggest rivals of its own Gemini team. This resource conflict reportedly even pushed two-billion-dollar researcher Noam Shazeer back to OpenAI. Ad

items.title: How Specializing the Vocabulary of SLMs Can Cut Inference Cost by 77% in Real Applications
items.content:
Models specialized for a domain or a task by fine-tuning general open-source models, such as Qwen and Gemma, inherit a vocabulary built for many domains and general applications.

In an essay grader we run in production, that vocabulary split the text the model writes most into many tokens. This article previews some results from the VocabX paper, which we will publish soon: how we specialized the vocabulary around the cost of each token rather than its frequency, and cut measured inference cost by 77% without changing the base model.

The tokenizer is usually treated as a fixed property of the base model, inherited and left alone. For a model specialized in a single domain, it can be one of the largest cost levers, and it is set before any training step.

One of the systems we run in production is an automated grader for Portuguese essays, built on Qwen3-4B. It receives the essay, the prompt and the supporting texts, and returns a JSON assessment with a grade and a comment for each competency.

The model was already small, at 4 billion parameters, and had already been trained for the task. Its tokenizer, however, was still the original Qwen3-4B one, built for many languages and many kinds of text. In the grader, it was used for a single language, Portuguese, and a single response format. That had two costs: the text the grader writes on every request took more tokens than it needed, and at every generated token the model scored a vocabulary of 151,669 entries, including many this task almost never uses.

We rebuilt that vocabulary with a method we call VocabX, keeping the same base model, the same data and the same training recipe. The numbers in this article come from the current version of the paper, still under review, and may change before publication.

The leading language models read and write in tokens, and the tokenizer decides how text becomes tokens. The tokenizers of the leading general-purpose models are trained on large collections of text from many domains and languages, from source code to contracts to Chinese. For a general-purpose model, that choice makes sense.

For a model used in a single domain, it creates two kinds of waste at once.

The first is fragmentation. The tokenizer splits into many pieces exactly what the domain repeats most. In the grader, every response starts with the same JSON envelope, the same competency names, the same evaluation phrases. In contracts, it is the boilerplate clauses. In code, the identifiers. Each of these sequences costs several tokens where one would do, and the model pays for every one of them on every request.

The second is excess. The vocabulary carries tens of thousands of entries the domain never uses, and the model computes a score for all of them at every token it generates. A model tuned to grade American school biology exams will almost never write in Chinese, yet it computes the probability of every Chinese-language token at every step. The vocabulary splits into many pieces what the domain repeats most, and carries entries the domain never uses.

The natural reaction is to count tokens and try to reduce the count. But the count is not the bill.

To see why a generated token costs more, it helps to look at how inference works. It has two phases. In prefill , the model processes the whole input in a single pass through the network: each weight read from GPU memory is reused for every input token, and the limit is compute. In decode , the model generates the response one token at a time, and each token needs a full pass. Each weight read is used only a few times, and the GPU spends most of its time waiting for data to arrive from memory: the limit becomes memory bandwidth.

items.title: PHP says AI review of critical bugs first sparked alarm in August, but signs surfaced in 2024
items.summary: In a lengthy statement about two critical vulnerabilities, the PHP Foundation explained how one dated to 2024, how a recent third-party review by AI companies heightened attention on both, why it scrambled to post information earlier than planned.
items.content:
PHP says AI review of critical bugs first sparked alarm in August, but signs surfaced in 2024

The two PHP vulnerabilities causing worldwide alarm first drew serious attention in August after an outside review by AI companies, the PHP Foundation explained in a lengthy statement on Wednesday.

The organization said the history of one bug, CVE-2026-109618, dates back to 2024, when PHP underwent its first external security audit in several years, but officials took no action.

The issue caused controversy within PHP as engineers debated how to address it, with concerns ranging from “backward compatibility breaks, new denial-of-service potential, or requiring changes to many third-party extensions which seemed impossible to coordinate.”

“The PHP security team, operating on consensus, struggled to choose between these and feared the repercussions of shipping the wrong choice,” the nonprofit foundation said .

“Combined with the lack of a known path to remote code execution and the small team of core developers with the necessary deep knowledge of the engine occupied with many responsibilities, this decision process caused work on a fix to stall and restart repeatedly over months.”

Hundreds of websites were taken offline on Wednesday by companies and governments as a result of CVE-2026-109618 and a related bug, CVE-2026-109619. Some are labeling them jointly as PHP2Shell.

Some estimates show that more than 70% of all websites on the internet use PHP. Internet infrastructure company Cloudflare reported seeing attempted exploitation.

The PHP Foundation said both vulnerabilities “sit in parts of PHP that nearly every request touches.”

“Their central place in PHP is what made both vulnerabilities serious, and also so hard to fix without breaking compatibility, hurting performance, or forcing changes on the large ecosystem of third-party extensions,” they said.

The scope of the vulnerabilities has alarmed cybersecurity defenders and governments , with a VirusTotal analysis showing 5.1 million IP addresses identified as running PHP. At least 758,000 IP addresses were disclosed as end-of-life PHP versions and 85,000 IP addresses were running the latest PHP releases available before developers issued emergency patches Wednesday morning.

These figures represent PHP's internet-facing footprint, not confirmed vulnerable systems. The patches only apply to versions dating back to PHP 8.2. Every version older than that no longer receives updates from the PHP Project.

Cisco Talos’ released estimates suggesting roughly 50% of vulnerable PHP systems may not receive a patch.

After deciding against taking any action in 2024, the PHP Foundation was confronted with the issues again with the emergence of powerful AI code review tools. Services from Anthropic and OpenAI were used earlier this year to scan PHP platforms and eventually a researcher at cybersecurity firm Calif reported the bugs on August 11.

On social media, Calif also credited another researcher with initially discovering the vulnerability and developing an exploit.

OpenAI and security companies Wiz and Trail of Bits also found the same vulnerabilities during audits of PHP.

The reports “made the full impact of the … problem clear, and from August 11th onward, fixing it became the top priority for all of the PHP Foundation's team working on security,” the foundation explained.

The PHP Foundation said its coordinated disclosure process was running smoothly until rumors of the bugs began to emerge on social media two days ago. They moved up their disclosure of the bugs by one day but argued that they could not have immediately released it because the fix was still being packaged.

They noted that Calif “mistakenly published a video” that showed their proof of concept working against a number of targets and revealed additional details about the vulnerabilities. That video , even after being deleted, began circulating and “accelerated development” of exploitation proof of concepts…

items.content:
아마존에 이어 구글도 기존 AI 개발 도구를 자체 칩에서 손쉽게 사용할 수 있도록 소프트웨어 생태계 확장에 나섰다. 개발자들이 익숙한 파이토치(PyTorch) 코드를 큰 수정 없이 자체 칩으로 옮길 수 있도록 지원해, 엔비디아 GPU와 CUDA 중심의 개발 환경에서 하드웨어 선택지를 넓히려는 움직임이다.

구글은 20일(현지시간) 열린 '파이토치 컨퍼런스 2026'에서 TPU용 파이토치 소프트웨어 스택인 ' 토치TPU(TorchTPU) '를 오픈소스로 공개했다.

아마존도 전날 자체 AI 칩 트레이니엄(Trainium)에서 기존 파이토치 코드를 실행하는 ‘토치뉴런(TorchNeuron)’을 발표했다. 아마존은 설정 하나를 바꾸는 방식으로 코드를 다시 작성하지 않고도 트레이니엄을 사용할 수 있다고 설명했으며, 20일부터 공개 베타로 제공한다.

파이토치는 AI 모델 개발과 학습에 널리 쓰이는 오픈소스 프레임워크다. 그동안 엔비디아 GPU와 CUDA에 맞춰 구축한 코드와 도구가 많아 다른 칩으로 옮기려면 추가 작업이 필요했다. 두 회사는 이 전환 부담을 줄여 자체 칩의 활용 폭을 넓히겠다는 것이다.

메타의 파이토치 개발팀과 공동 개발한 토치TPU는 기존 파이토치 API를 유지하면서 TPU에서 모델 학습과 추론, 배포를 지원한다. 개발자는 최소한의 코드 변경으로 기존 애플리케이션을 TPU에서 실행할 수 있다.

일반 실행 모드에서 모델 오류를 확인한 뒤 ‘torch.compile’을 활용해 성능을 최적화할 수 있으며, 분산 학습 기능과 진단 도구도 기본 지원한다.

구글은 모델 실행뿐 아니라 학습과 추론에 쓰이는 주요 도구까지 TPU에 연결했다. 허깅페이스와 협력해 트랜스포머스(Transformers) v5에서 ‘device_map="tpu"’ 설정으로 모델을 TPU에 배치할 수 있도록 했다.

이미지 생성 모델 개발 도구인 디퓨저스(Diffusers)도 TPU에서 일반 실행 모드와 컴파일 최적화, 여러 칩에 모델을 나눠 실행하는 텐서 병렬 처리를 지원한다. 허깅페이스 모델을 TPU 인프라에서 지속적으로 테스트하는 체계도 구축했다.

대규모 모델 추론 도구인 ‘vLLM’과 ‘SGLang’의 TPU 지원도 강화했다. 인퍼랙트(Inferact), 라딕스아크(RadixArk)와 각각 협력해 TPU용 백엔드를 마련했으며, 기존 스케줄러와 API 서버 등은 유지하면서 TPU에 맞춰 연산을 최적화하도록 했다.

여러 서버에 추론 작업을 배분하는 쿠버네티스 기반 시스템 ‘llm-d’도 1.0 버전으로 공개했다. 요청 처리에 필요한 문맥이 이미 저장된 서버로 작업을 보내고, 입력을 처리하는 프리필(prefill)과 답변을 생성하는 디코딩(decode)을 분리해 효율을 높인다. 구글 클라우드의 쿠버네티스 엔진(GKE)에서는 공통 인터페이스로 GPU와 TPU를 활용할 수 있다.

학습 분야에서는 대규모 분산 학습 프레임워크 ‘토치타이탄(TorchTitan)’에 TPU 지원을 통합했다. 구글은 ‘큐원 3 8B’ 모델 학습에서 칩의 이론상 연산 성능을 실제 학습에 얼마나 활용하는지 나타내는 모델 연산 활용률(MFU)이 최대 52%를 기록했다고 밝혔다. 또 ‘아이언우드(Ironwood)’ TPU를 8192개까지 늘렸을 때 칩 수 증가에 거의 비례하는 성능 향상을 확인했다고 설명했다.

강화학습 프레임워크 ‘VeRL’에도 TPU 백엔드와 참고용 학습 구성을 추가했다. ‘레이(Ray)’를 통해서는 데이터 처리와 학습, 강화학습, 추론 등 단계별로 CPU와 GPU, TPU를 배정해 하나의 작업 흐름에서 함께 사용할 수 있도록 했다.

개발자의 이전 작업을 돕는 'TPU 에이전트 스위트(TPU Agent Suite)'도 깃허브 에서 프리뷰 버전으로 제공한다. 이 도구는 플러그인 방식으로 개발 환경에 연결해 초기 설정과 오류 진단, 사용 관련 질문, 추론 성능 조정을 지원한다.

이와 함께 온디바이스 AI 추론 도구 ‘라이트RT(LiteRT)’와 파이토치 모델을 연결하는 ‘라이트RT-토치(LiteRT-Torch)’도 공개했다. 파이토치 모델을 변환해 안드로이드와 iOS, 윈도, 맥OS, 리눅스, 웹, 사물인터넷(IoT) 기기에서 실행하도록 지원하며, 기기의 CPU와 GPU, 신경망처리장치(NPU)를 활용할 수 있다.

items.title: Google Hardens Chrome Against ClickFix Attacks, Insecure HTTP Connections
items.summary: Protections have been added against scams and social engineering, including new site warnings and server-side Gemini analysis. The post Google Hardens Chrome Against ClickFix Attacks, Insecure HTTP Connections appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
Google has announced new Chrome protections against scams and social engineering, including new site warnings, server-side Gemini analysis, and detection of ClickFix commands.

The Gemini and ClickFix protections are part of Enhanced Protection, the Safe Browsing mode Google introduced in 2020 . Last year, the company said more than 1 billion Chrome users had turned it on.

Google claims Enhanced Protection makes users “ten times safer” than Standard Protection against phishing, social engineering, notification abuse, and other scams. The metric is based on how many safety warnings, on average, each group of users receives.

Chrome’s Safe Browsing site warnings now come in two levels, mirroring a model previously applied to file downloads. When Safe Browsing is highly confident a page is malicious, users still get the full-page red ‘dangerous site’ warning.

The new ‘suspicious site’ level covers lower-confidence verdicts. It flags pages that use deceptive tactics typical of known malicious sites. Because these warnings have their own design, Google says it can safely display more of them.

Gemini-powered scam detection has also moved to Google’s servers. The on-device version launched last year focused on tech support scams and was limited to Enhanced Protection users on supported devices. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

The more capable server-side model is now available to every Enhanced Protection user. It also targets additional threats, such as fake antivirus and fake browser update pages.

The model’s review of a page looks at signals such as the brand on display, the page’s purpose, and a scam likelihood score. “Safe Browsing then considers Gemini’s analysis, in combination with domain reputation and other security signals, to generate a final verdict,” Google explains.

The company says page text is only analyzed when a site shows strong signs of being a scam. Any page content that leaves the device is handled ephemerally and is not logged, stored, or used to train AI models.

In ClickFix attacks, victims are lured into pasting and running commands themselves. Those commands almost always invoke living-off-the-land binaries such as PowerShell. Since the malware download takes place in the terminal rather than the browser, Chrome and Safe Browsing download protections never come into play.

Chrome can now spot when Enhanced Protection users are manipulated into copying a suspicious command. “If a potential ClickFix script is copied, the clipboard payload is scrubbed of PII and sent to Safe Browsing for further analysis, and if a dangerous verdict is returned, Chrome shows a warning,” Google says .

“This system is designed to be high precision, in order to protect users in real time while minimizing disruption to legitimate developer activity,” the company adds.

Chrome now asks before connecting over HTTP

Chrome also now prompts users for approval before it connects to a site over unencrypted HTTP. Enhanced Protection users received the feature earlier this year. As promised last year , Google has now turned it on by default for everyone .

According to Google, the ‘Not Secure’ label alone falls short. Research shows that passive indicators like it can go unnoticed, and short-lived HTTP traffic such as redirects never receives the label at all. The bigger problem, the company says, is that the label only appears once the user’s data and connection are already exposed.

The prompt is shown on the first visit to an HTTP site. “Once the HTTP use is approved, Chrome will not warn again until the user has not visited the site for at least two weeks,” Google notes.

By default, sites that can’t obtain a publicly trusted HTTPS certificate don’t trigger warnings. Examples include single-label hostnames and local IP addresses. Google says these hosts are typically at lower risk, as an attacker would have to be on the same local network to tamper with the traffic.

items.title: PHP2Shell Patches Land as First Exploitation Attempts Hit Sensors
items.summary: Several cybersecurity companies saw exploitation attempts of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 before PHP released the patches. The post PHP2Shell Patches Land as First Exploitation Attempts Hit Sensors appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
PHP has rolled out patches for two critical-severity vulnerabilities named PHP2Shell that could provide attackers with unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE).

The issues are tracked as CVE-2026-109618 (out-of-memory (OOM) corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale global state) and have a CVSS score of 9.2. For both, RCE was confirmed on Apache with mod_php.

“Both issues sit in parts of PHP that nearly every request touches: memory management and error handling. Their central place in PHP is what made both vulnerabilities serious, and also so hard to fix,” the PHP Foundation says.

Patches for both were included in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, PHP 8.0, and PHP 8.1 were also released.

Before the fixes arrived, however, proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits targeting the two security defects started circulating.

Preemptive attack surface management firm WatchTowr says it has seen the first in-the-wild exploitation attempts hitting its sensors around the same time the patches landed, but has not observed successful attempts. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

“Whilst nobody has been successful to date, we don’t expect that will last long,” WatchTowr head of threat intelligence Jake Knott said.

Several other companies reported seeing exploitation attempts, including before the patches landed.

“We are now seeing php2shell exploited in the wild at scale. Most of the attacks we observe abuse PHP’s session upload-progress path, and we expect more exploit paths to appear before and after the fix ships,” Hadrian reported a few hours before the fixes were released.

Patchstack and Cloudflare also observed exploitation attempts earlier in the day. Vega saw exploit attempts in the wild that leveraged a public PoC.

According to PHP’s maintainers, all PHP installations that handle web requests are potentially at risk of exploitation, “including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed”.

Where patching is not possible, users can implement measures that “reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe,” the PHP Foundation says.

The two PHP2Shell flaws affect nearly all PHP releases back to version 5.4. They can also be exploited to read sensitive process memory, which may contain credentials, API keys, and other secrets.

“This is a goldmine for hackers. They can hijack real websites to take advantage of the site’s reputation to do things like phish people, serve malicious software from the trusted channel; the opportunities are endless,” Malwarebytes global head of scam and AI research Shahak Shalev said.

Wiz, along with OpenAI and Calif , discovered the vulnerabilities in August and kept them contained until patches were developed and distributed across the ecosystem.

“These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” Wiz notes.

Calif explains that an initial OOM flaw in PHP was discovered in 2020, and then rediscovered during a PHP audit in 2024. Because exploitation was not proven, however, it was not patched. Courtesy of frontier AI models, the OOM weakness could be better analyzed and eventually turned into RCE.

The OOM to RCE issue was independently reported by Calif and OpenAI on August 11. Additional attack vectors were later reported by OpenAI and Wiz.

“The reports from Calif, OpenAI, and Wiz made the full impact of the OOM problem clear, and from August 11th onward, fixing it became the top priority for all of the PHP Foundation’s team working on security,” the PHP Foundation notes.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Agent Removed Safety Monitoring, Then Falsely Denied Doing So
items.summary: OpenAI has revealed that two artificial intelligence (AI) agents powered by GPT-6.1 Sol and one GPT-6 Astra weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes during two internal coding tasks. The AI company said the incident took place on October 3 and 6, 2
items.content:
OpenAI has revealed that two artificial intelligence (AI) agents powered by GPT-6.1 Sol and one GPT-6 Astra weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes during two internal coding tasks.

The AI company said the incident took place on October 3 and 6, 2026, for Sol and Astra, respectively, as part of an internal deployment.

"A GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to our Security team, treating an earlier instruction not to send messages during a Slack history search as a reason to suppress monitoring notifications," OpenAI said in a report.

The end result of this action was that the misalignment monitor still ran and saved its reports, but automatic human alerts were disabled by setting "no_notify" to true and emptying the lists of people configured to receive monitoring reports.

In another task on October 6, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program is said to have removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, and then falsely claimed to the user that the functionality had not been removed.

"No [...] I did not remove an enabled monitor from it," the final response from the agent reads.

OpenAI said, in both cases, the AI agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be retained, but ultimately chose not to do so after interpreting routine coding instructions as "permission to weaken them."

In response to the findings, the company said it's strengthening its misalignment monitoring system and assessing if these scenarios are an outlier or whether they demonstrate a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring.

"In addition to making it harder for models to disable monitoring [during evaluations], we are looking to understand why models might seek to do so in the first place," OpenAI said. "It is possible that this behavior is simply an example of 'benign' overpersistence, with models not understanding why monitoring is important or insisting that instructions be executed beyond what a reasonable person might expect."

The disclosure is the latest instance of AI agents acting in ways their developers did not intend to. Last week, the ChatGPT-maker disclosed seven misalignment incidents, including one case where an internal research model stole cryptocurrency from a wallet it did not own to pay the fees needed to deploy smart contracts on Ethereum's Sepolia test network and failed to report that it took the funds without permission.

It also comes amid growing concerns that the development of increasingly powerful AI systems is outpacing safety efforts, leading to warnings that this could make it harder to monitor and control them as they gain greater autonomy.

Earlier this week, Microsoft announced new controls to monitor and contain potentially rogue AI agents in enterprise environments as part of Project Perception , a continuously learning AI-powered cyber defense system the company unveiled in July 2026.

"Models have been trained to attain results, which often leads to reward hacking, and models are not optimized around organizational norms or judgment," Hayete Gallot, executive vice president of Microsoft Security, said . "Agents are unpredictable. They will adapt as the context changes, may not behave as intended, and will collaborate and collude with other agents to reach their objectives, without needing to be compromised."

With agents often having extensive permissions to access data, tools, and systems, not to mention take actions and make decisions on their own, Redmond said they pose a new kind of insider security risk that requires continuous monitoring.

items.title: OpenAI agents disabled safety monitoring, one lied about it
items.summary: OpenAI agents powered by the GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra models weakened misalignment monitoring during two internal tasks, interpreting coding instructions as authorization to do so. [...]
items.content:
OpenAI agents disabled safety monitoring, one lied about it

OpenAI agents powered by the GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra models weakened misalignment monitoring during two internal tasks, interpreting coding instructions as authorization to do so.

AI alignment refers to how well an AI system’s goals and behavior align with human values, intentions, and instructions. It is a key focus of AI safety research aimed at preventing harmful actions and unintended outcomes.

One of the incidents occurred on October 3, when an agent powered by GPT-6.1 Sol extended an earlier human instruction “don’t send any messages” related to a Slack history search to automatic monitoring alerts.

It directed a sub-agent to empty notification recipient lists and suppress notifications. Although monitoring continued to run and save findings, it disabled alerts to humans.

OpenAI says this happened even though the agent earlier reasoned that alerts should remain enabled.

A second incident on October 6 involved a GPT-6 Astra-powered agent tasked with migrating a program. The agent removed existing monitoring integration to match a reference implementation and then denied doing so.

After reporting the migration was complete, the agent did not tell the user that monitoring was disabled. Furthermore, when asked directly, the agent lied to the human.

GPT-6 Astra agent denies disabling monitoring

OpenAI says that the agent also replaced a test intended to preserve monitoring with one asserting that the monitor context was absent.

Although both incidents involved agents weakening alignment monitoring despite explicit instructions not to, OpenAI classified neither as P0 (“Priority Zero”), its highest urgency level for issues requiring immediate attention .

OpenAI says it is investigating whether the unintended behavior stems from excessive persistence in task-completion goals, a poor understanding of monitoring requirements, or a specific tendency to evade monitoring.

“We are also developing evaluations to test whether models might have a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular and exhibit motivated reasoning in order to do so,” OpenAI explained.

“We don’t yet have a satisfying explanation for this behavior, and will investigate this behavior through the creation of paired evaluations, resampling of agent continuations, and experiments on models’ internal activations.”

The AI firm says it has updated its internal Auto-Review system to now detect and block attempts to disable misalignment monitoring. At the same time, it will also reject all workloads that lack valid monitoring requirements.

Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked

Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

‘Context Bombs’ Cut AI Attack Success by Misleading Agents With Fake Targets
items.summary: Deceptive prompts lure AI agents into decoys and dead ends, cutting attack success by up to 91% in tests and raising the cost of a successful attack 23-fold. The post ‘Context Bombs’ Cut AI Attack Success by Misleading Agents With Fake Targets appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
London- and New York-based Tracebit has developed a military style solution to AI attacks. Just as landmines are used to destroy or slow an advancing army, Tracebit has developed AI ‘context bombs’ that are planted in the battlefield. Each bomb comprises crafted and hidden prompts that are automatically ingested by the attacking AI when it crawls the target. These new prompts interfere with the original, possibly malign, purpose of the attacking agent.

Tracebit’s new research ( Making attacking agents pay ’) extends earlier research that used different context bombs to trigger guardrails. It now focuses on misdirecting and entrapping the agents with fake targets and deceptively complex problems. To achieve this, Tracebit developed nine new context techniques (ingested fake prompts) that stopped all GPT 5.6 Cyber, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8 Max, and DeepSeek V4 Pro attacks. The same bombs also worked against Frontier Models, cutting GPT-6 Astra’s successes by 54% and nearly quadrupling its bill per attack. The effect against Claude Opus 5 was even more obvious: attack success was cut by 91%.

The single most effective of the nine prompt bombs was a fake pen testing report. It presented itself as a recent assessment, labeled real attack paths as canaries, and described decoys as valuable targets that had already been exploited. In many cases it made the AI believe the defender’s real systems were traps – so it avoided them, reducing the achieved objectives by 58%. Some agents accepted the warnings and stopped early, leaving exploitable targets untouched. Across Cyber, Kimi, Qwen and DeepSeek, runs reaching an objective fell from 39 / 40 at baseline to 2 / 40.

Other bombs include an unending web service, apparent passwords locked behind layer after layer of encryption, and an endless database. In this last deception, every page pointed to another page. “GLM-5.3 crawled 825 pages in 55 minutes, spotted the trap, tried other leads, and still came back for one more try,” comment the researchers.

Combining the bombs had the best overall effect. None of the Chinese models from Moonshot, Alibaba and DeepSeek achieved their objectives when all nine bombs were deployed.

Even if the context bomb failed to stop an attack, it increased the cost of each success by 23x. Attackers may have deep pockets, but they are not limitless. There comes a point where the value of the target simply isn’t worth the cost of the attack. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Tracebit’s neutralizing prompt injections are effectively the opposite of malicious prompt injection attacks. Even if this occurs from an external attacker, the internal context bombs are the most recent prompts that should usurp the attacker’s intent.

Andy Smith, co-founder and CEO at Tracebit, explains the arguments: “We’ve seen in recent attacks that AI models exhibit unsanctioned and deceptive behaviors – the best defense against that is to beat them at their own game. This means adopting deception to send them down rabbit holes and tie them up in knots, so they burn time and tokens while avoiding real targets. By inflating the cost 23x it asks the attacker, ‘is this worth it’, meanwhile the agents run erratically which makes them more likely to trigger alarms – alerting defenders to a problem and giving them more time to respond.”

items.content:
시스코가 에이전틱 AI(Agentic AI) 확산에 따른 기업의 비용 관리 및 운영 과제를 담은 '2026 스플렁크 옵저버빌리티 현황 보고서: AI 시대의 예측 가능성 회복'을 발표했다.

이번 보고서는 전 세계 10개국의 IT 운영 및 엔지니어링 전문가 2,050명을 대상으로 진행한 조사 결과를 바탕으로 작성됐다.

조사에 따르면, 기업들이 AI 에이전트를 도입하는 속도에 비해 이를 효과적으로 모니터링하고 관리할 수 있는 역량은 충분하지 않은 것으로 나타났다. 응답자의 83%는 AI 에이전트 활용에 따른 예상치 못한 결과를 우려했으며, 에이전트의 행동을 모니터링하고 통제하는 에이전트 옵저버빌리티의 필요성이 커졌다.

기업들이 AI 에이전트 모니터링의 중요성을 인식하고 있음에도 실제 성능과 비즈니스 성과를 체계적으로 관리하는 데 어려움을 겪고 있다. 응답자의 87%는 AI 모니터링을 조직의 우선순위로 꼽았으나 54%는 명확한 비즈니스 성과 목표를 세우지 못했다고 답했다. 대규모 언어 모델의 응답 품질이나 AI 환각 현상을 효과적으로 모니터링하는 데 한계를 겪는다는 응답도 과반을 넘었다.

AI 사용량이 늘어나면서 비용 예측의 어려움도 가중됐다. 응답자의 55%는 향후 사용 규모를 예측하기 어려워 AI 비용을 정확하게 통제하지 못한다고 답했다. 높은 기본 운영 비용보다 예상치 못한 비용 급증이 조직 운영에 더 큰 부담을 주는 것으로 나타났다.

AI 에이전트가 IT 인프라 전반으로 활용 범위를 넓히면서 IT 운영, 엔지니어링, 보안 조직 간 협업도 강화되는 추세다. 응답자의 81%는 AI 워크로드 모니터링을 계기로 옵저버빌리티팀과 보안팀 간 협업이 증가했다고 답했다. 두 조직 간 데이터 공유 비율 역시 높아져 실시간 문제 진단과 대응을 뒷받침하고 있다.

items.title: High-Severity Flaws Exploited in Three Days as Ransomware Dominates Q3: Rapid7
items.summary: Rapid7’s Q3 analysis finds high-severity flaws exploited within three days on average, while AI appeared in just 8% of tracked incidents. The post High-Severity Flaws Exploited in Three Days as Ransomware Dominates Q3: Rapid7 appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
High-severity flaws are exploited faster; ransomware remains the dominant threat; the US is the world’s most targeted country, and attacks increasingly involve the use of AI (but largely manually rather than autonomously).

Rapid7’s threat analysis for Q3, 2026 adds color to these basic details of the current threat landscape.

During Q3, high-severity vulnerabilities were exploited within an average of three days from disclosure, with 71% exploited during the first seven days. Seventy-nine percent of these vulnerabilities are classed by Rapid7 as ‘holy grail’ flaws (that is, remote and requiring neither credentials nor local user involvement).

Ransomware remains a primary threat throughout the world. The most targeted sectors in Q3 were business services, manufacturing, and healthcare. The US was the most targeted nation (60% of attacks), followed by Germany (7%), Italy (5%) and Canada (5%).

The most successful ransomware groups were The Gentlemen (342 claimed incidents) and Qilin (339). INC Ransom was third with 99, followed by DeadLock (98), and Krybit (95).

Government sector victims of ransomware are increasing (up 15% on the previous three months) and are also focused on the US (with its share growing from 33% in Q2 to 45% in Q3). Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

The expected use of AI in attacks is beginning to show, but perhaps more slowly than forecasted or feared. “The finding I’d put in front of anyone is that AI showed up as an operational component in only 8% of the incidents we tracked. That’s interesting because the board-deck version of this year has been wall-to-wall AI attackers, and the data doesn’t support that story,” Douglas McKee, director of vulnerability intelligence at Rapid7 told SecurityWeek .

According to the report from Rapid7 , only 8% of tracked incidents cited AI as an operational component, and this is not yet fully autonomous. “Humans still chose what to attack and why in every documented case,” says the report. What is growing, however, is automation of the ‘tactical middle’ of the attack chain: technique selection, target triage, and recovering from a failed step can all now run without a human being present.

“The piece people keep mashing together is AI finding flaws versus AI exploiting them. Finding is real, and it’s accelerating. The AI exploitation wave everyone is bracing for didn’t show up in our data this quarter.”

Defenders, suggests Rapid7, should monitor AI API usage patterns from unexpected hosts and processes as a telemetry source; that is, actively look for unusual or unauthorized use of AI tools within the environment.

For their part, attackers attempt to avoid detection by using fragmented, multi-session prompting to bypass AI provider safeguards. While single-session malicious requests are often blocked, splitting objectives across multiple sessions can evade detection.

During Q3, the researchers tracked 15 separate nation-state (APT) and cybercrime groups. Noteworthy examples include ENERGETIC BEAR, Void Blizzard, and Sandworm which are all Russia linked. APT31 is China linked, Lazarus is North Korea, and Operation C-Major is Pakistan.

Government organizations are the core target for APT groups. Other sectors include defense, transportation, media, healthcare, aerospace, finance, energy, and technology. Among the attackers, the research discloses a previously undocumented Linux toolkit (a backdoor named ‘ted’ compiled into a trojanized HAProxy build, an SSH keylogger, and a curl-based RAT) used by the DPRK against South Korean organizations since early 2025. The Operation C-Major group has been active since the mid-2010s and focuses on using phishing and mobile spyware for espionage against Indian military and diplomatic staff.
